39.zh:
耶穌叫眾人散去，就上船，來到馬加丹的境界。

**馬加丹**。馬可福音是大瑪努他（可8:10）。可能有幾個不同的名稱。大多數現代權威支持讀作馬格大拉，並且暫時認爲它是Mejdel，在加利利海西岸，迦百農和提比哩亞之間。Mejdel的遺迹位於革尼撒勒平原南部邊界附近。

24.zh:
耶穌說：「我奉差遣不過是到以色列家迷失的羊那裏去。」

**我奉差遣，不過是**。見對第21節的註釋。即，耶穌主要是奉差到猶太人那裏去的，可是一有機會他也不拒絕把他給自己百姓的祝福給外邦人（見本註釋第四册原文第26-30頁）。直到基督升到天上許多年之後，猶太基督徒們才完全領會了，上帝認爲各地的所有人都適合成爲天國公民的事實（見徒9:9-18,32-35；10:1-48；15:1-29；羅1:16；9:24等）。
**迷失的羊**。見對@太10:6@的註釋。

38.zh:
吃的人，除了婦女孩子，共有四千。

**四千男人**。在使5,000人吃飽時，加上婦人孩子共有10,000多人在場（見《歷》第八十五章）。如果現在的比例也是一樣，就會有8,000多人在場，包括男人，婦女和孩子。

34.zh:
耶穌說：「你們有多少餅？」他們說：「有七個，還有幾條小魚。」

**有多少餅**。關於在使5,000人吃飽時所提出的類似問題，以及「餅」的註釋，見對@可6:38@的註釋。
**幾條小魚**。魚並不多，並且在門徒們看來，它們是那麽小，幾乎都不值得注意。

37.zh:
眾人都吃，並且吃飽了，收拾剩下的零碎，裝滿了七個筐子。

**衆人都吃**。見對@可6:42@的註釋。
**零碎**。關於「零碎」這個詞，見對@可6:43@的註釋。
**筐子**。希臘文spurides，由草繩或枝條編成了大籃子（見對@可6:43@的註釋）。

32.zh:
耶穌叫門徒來，說：「我憐憫這眾人，因為他們同我在這裏已經三天，也沒有吃的了。我不願意叫他們餓著回去，恐怕在路上困乏。」

**叫門徒來**。[使四千人吃飽，太15:32-39=可8:1-10。主要的註釋在：馬太福音。見「從公開傳道到退隱時期」；「主耶穌的傳道生涯」；關於神蹟，見本册註釋原文第208-213頁。] 關於緊接在此之前的事件，見對太15:21的註釋。關於這個神蹟的附近地區，和在同一地區從前行過的一個神蹟以及這兩個事件之間的關係，見對@可5:1,18-20@的註釋。關於這兩個事件的比較，見對本章末尾的附註。時間很可能在公元30年的早夏，可能在六月底或七月初。
**憐憫**。救主總是被人類的苦難和悲哀打動（來4:15）。
**衆人**。即使不都是外邦人，大部分也是外邦人（《歷》第四十四章）。他們最初對耶穌懷有偏見，現在似乎不僅友好地待他，而且對他所說的非常感興趣了。
**三天**。根據東方的計算方法，這可能是一個整天，加上這天之前的一部分和之後的一部分（見本册註釋原文第248-250頁）。人們可能至少帶了一天否則就是兩天的食物，因爲耶穌直到第三天才對之感到關心。
**我不願**。直譯是，「我不樂意」。
**恐怕他們困乏**。他們餓了，耶穌關心他們身體的康樂，就像他關心他們屬靈的福利一樣。

21.zh:
耶穌離開那裏，退到推羅、西頓的境內去。

**耶穌離開那裏**。[退到腓尼基，太15:21-28=可7:24-30。主要的註釋在：馬太福音。見「從公開傳道到退隱時期」；「基督服務的持續時間，加利利傳道時期的開始，主耶穌的傳道生涯」；關於神蹟，見本册註釋原文第208-213頁。] 接下來的事件很可能發生在公元30年晚春，可能約在五月份。加利利傳道因使5,000人吃飽和在迦百農會堂裏關於生命糧的布道（見對@約6:1,25@的註釋）達到了高潮。大衆性的潮流開始轉而反對耶穌了，就像一年前在猶太地一樣（見《歷》第四十一章），那些自認爲是他的跟從者的人多數都拒絕了他（見對@約6:60-66@的註釋）。這是在那年的逾越節之前不過幾天的時候，耶穌沒有參加那個逾越節（見對@可7:1@的註釋）。
第三次加利利旅行布道曾使猶太領袖們大大驚慌（見《歷》第四十二章；見對@可6:14@的註釋）。在逾越節後，一個代表團從耶路撒冷來到耶穌那裏，控告他正在違反宗教規條（見可7:1-23）。但是他通過揭露他們的假冒爲善使他們無言可答，他們就氣憤憤地走了（見《歷》第四十二章）。他們的態度和威脅說明他的性命有危險了（《歷》第四十三章）。所以與他先前給門徒們的忠告相一致，他就暫時退出了加利利（見對@太10:14,23@的註釋），就像他一年前在猶太地被領袖們拒絕時離開那裏一樣（見對@太4:12@的註釋）。
這次向北撤退標志著基督傳道的一個新時期的開始，也標志著他在加利利傳道的結束，約從公元29年的逾越節到公元30年的逾越節，他曾在加利利獻身傳道約一年之久。當時距他的死期已經不到一年了。
雖然與耶路撒冷來的文士和法利賽人産生衝突，是促使耶穌退到腓尼基地區的直接原因，但這次的旅行也有它積極的一面。耶穌有一個明確的目的，不僅在於離開加利利，而且在於轉到腓尼基的一般地區。既然他已經被猶太地和加利利的猶太人拒絕了，耶穌就尋求一個機會教導他的門徒們爲非猶太人作工。異教徒需要福音，他現在開始進行的一系列教訓，計劃是要使門徒們認識到異教徒的需要，以及他們也是天國預期之候選人的事實。退到腓尼基給這樣的教導提供了一個絕好的機會（見《歷》第四十三章）。在這次訪問腓尼基期間，耶穌只行了一個神蹟。然而，這次訪問顯然不具有那三次加利利旅行布道的意義，因爲耶穌一到那裏就隱退了，並且計劃不讓人知道他在那裏（見可7:24）。
**境內**。希臘文merē，「區域」，「分界綫」或「地區」。耶穌退到了加利利與腓尼基接壤的丘陵中（見《歷》第四十三章），從那裏他可以看到推羅和西頓的城市，相隔23英里（約37千米），在下麵的濱海平原。該地區屬於羅馬的叙利亞省（見本註釋第二册原文第69頁）。
**推羅和西頓**。見本册註釋第一册原文第128頁；本註釋第二册原文第67,68頁；見對@創10:15@的註釋。在羅馬人來到之前，數百年來腓尼基人曾一直是世界貿易的領導者。

35.zh:
他就吩咐眾人坐在地上，

**地**。關於沒有像在使5,000人吃飽的叙述中一樣提到草的重要事實，見對本章結尾的附註。

28.en: Great is thy faith. She has met the test; her faith stands firm. She is certain that it is within the power of Christ to bestow the gift of health to her daughter. Compare Christ’s commendation of the centurion (see on Luke 7:9). That very hour. Like the nobleman’s son (see John 4:43–54) and the centurion’s servant (see Luke 7:1–10), the daughter of the Canaanite woman was healed at a distance, not in Christ’s immediate presence, and as in each of the other cases, healing was immediate, complete.
28.zh:
耶穌說：「婦人，你的信心是大的！照你所要的，給你成全了吧。」從那時候，她女兒就好了。

**你的信心是大的**。她已經面對了考驗；她的信心是堅定的。她確信基督有能力把健康賜給她的女兒。請比較基督對那個百夫長的稱讚（見對@路7:9@的註釋）。
**那時候**。像那個大臣的兒子（見約4:43-54）和百夫長的僕人一樣（見路7:1-10），這個迦南婦人的女兒在遠處就被治好了，並不直接在基督面前，並且與在另外兩個案例中一樣，都是立即、完全治愈的。

13.zh:
耶穌回答說：「凡栽種的物，若不是我天父栽種的，必要拔出來。

**凡栽種的物**。這裏的意思指每一條遺傳，每一條「人的吩咐」（見對@可7:3,13,15@的註釋）。

33.zh:
門徒說：「我們在這野地，哪里有這麼多的餅叫這許多人吃飽呢？」

**門徒說**。請比較@可6:35-37@的註釋。

14.zh:
任憑他們吧！他們是瞎眼領路的；若是瞎子領瞎子，兩個人都要掉在坑裏。」

**溝**。更可說是：「坑」或「洞」。

22.zh:
有一個迦南婦人，從那地方出來，喊著說：「主啊，大衛的子孫，可憐我！我女兒被鬼附得甚苦。」

**一個迦南婦人**。腓尼基人是古時的迦南民族；實際上，他們稱自己是迦南人（見對@創10:6,18@的註釋）。希臘人稱他們是腓尼基人，顯然是以一種紫色染料的名稱（希臘文phoinix）命名的，那種染料是腓尼基人很早以前，在愛琴海地區做貿易時希臘人從他們買進的（見本註釋第二册原文第68頁）。迦南人是含族血統，但在他們居住在巴勒斯坦初期時，就採用了閃族語系並且吸收了那麽多閃族文化，以致於長期以來就被認爲他們是閃族出身了。猶太人是閃族人，希伯來人和迦南人在語言和一般的文化特徵方面極其類似。
這是記載在福音書中的關於耶穌曾照顧非猶太人的第四個場合。第一個是在撒瑪利亞的叙加（約4:5-42），第二個是在迦百農（路7:1-10），第三個是在格拉森附近地區（可5:1-20）。當然，撒瑪利亞是部分的猶太人，雖然耶穌爲他們傳道不會被看作可支持的，但也不會給他帶來爲徹頭徹尾的外邦人傳道的責難。那百夫長待猶太人如同朋友，並且相信他們持有的是真信仰。基督爲百夫長行的神蹟是依照猶太領袖們的要求而行的。治好格拉森被鬼附的人，不可能被猶太人解釋爲，基督故意和異教徒接觸。反而，他們可能會認爲是强加在基督身上的一個緊急事件，在某種意義上，他趕出那些鬼乃是出於自衛。而且，他不肯讓那兩個脫離了被鬼附的人作爲門徒與他聯合。即使在現在，關於這個腓尼基婦人，耶穌也沒有公開地爲那地區的人作工（見可7:24）。她來到他面前並將自己的請求强加給他。
基督與巴勒斯坦的非猶太人交往，他只是爲「以色列家迷失的羊」（太15:24）傳道的附帶事件。如果他爲選民的勞苦偶遇任何程度的成功，他就有必要至少在表面上遵照傳統到這種程度,以致猶太領袖們不該有任何機會控告他，毀掉他們已經建立起來反對外邦人的隔墻，因爲那些隔墻在許多方面都是錯誤的（見本註釋第四册原文第28-33頁）。否則，他就會破壞自己爲之勞苦的百姓的影響力。現今，基督徒工人們要認爲所有人在上帝面前都是平等的，並且要謹記「上帝並不偏待人」（徒10:34）。
**那地方**。希臘文horia，「邊界」，這裏指被各邊界圍繞之地（見對第21節的註釋）。耶穌是在推羅和西頓的附近，那婦人是推羅和西頓地區的人，這裏所記載的事件發生在同一個地區內。那婦人一發現耶穌就來「俯伏在他脚前」（可7:25），她俯伏在他面前，這在東方通常是一個人向長者提出請求時所采取的姿勢（見對@太4:9；8:2@的註釋）。
**可憐**。希臘文eleeō（見對@太5:7@的註釋）。
**大衛的子孫**。見對@太1:1@的註釋。一個外邦婦人竟然用這個頭銜稱呼耶穌，暗示承認他是彌賽亞，實在令人驚奇。有許多猶太人住在腓尼基，在他們中間早就開始流傳著關於耶穌的奇妙事迹了（見可3:8；路6:17）。顯然通過這些住在腓尼基的猶太人，那婦人曾聽說過耶穌（見《歷》第四十三章）。
**被鬼附得甚苦**。直譯是，「嚴重地被鬼附著」，或，更爲自由地譯爲「嚴重地被一個魔鬼附著」（見對可第一章的附註）。

1.zh:
那時，有法利賽人和文士從耶路撒冷來見耶穌，說：

**那時**。[有關遺傳與儀文污穢之爭，太15:1-20=可7:1-23。主要的註釋在：馬可福音。] 關於馬太使用「那時」這個詞的註釋，見對@太4:1@的註釋。

25.zh:
那婦人來拜他，說：「主啊，幫助我！」

**拜**。直譯是，「俯伏自己」（見對@太8:2@的註釋）。在敬拜的對像面前，或者在人面前，尤其是在向之尋求恩待的長者面前，都可以采取這個典型的東方懇求姿勢（見對@斯3:2@的註釋）這個婦人使用彌賽亞的稱號「大衛的子孫」（見對@太1:1@；15:22的註釋）暗示她至少模糊地認識到了耶穌實際是誰。並不清楚她用這個稱呼只是因爲她的猶太鄰舍曾用它來討論基督的奇妙作爲，還是表示她本人在一定程度上相信耶穌就是彌賽亞。

30.zh:
有許多人到他那裏，帶著瘸子、瞎子、啞巴、有殘疾的，和好些別的病人，都放在他腳前；他就治好了他們。

**都放在他脚前**。不是以一種粗魯的方式，而顯然是以一種决定性的方式。他們把病人和受苦的人都托付給他的憐憫。

36.zh:
拿著這七個餅和幾條魚，祝謝了，擘開，遞給門徒；門徒又遞給眾人。

**祝謝了**。見對@可6:41@的註釋。

27.zh:
婦人說：「主啊，不錯；但是狗也吃它主人桌子上掉下來的碎渣兒。」

**主啊，不錯**。或，「是的，主」。在耶穌假裝對她熱切的請求漠不關心的背後（見對太15:23,26的註釋），她顯然察覺到了涌自他源源不盡之偉大愛心的溫柔同情。他屈尊與她討論這個問題，而不是像拉比們做的那樣斷然拒絕她，這事本身顯然給了她勇氣相信他會同意她的請求。他的聲音沒帶有一點兒不耐煩，並且他的面容顯示出的只是他面上常有的平靜、尊嚴和無限的親切。
**碎渣兒**。希臘文psichia，一個小辭形式，意思是「一點兒」，或「碎屑」。就連「小狗」（見對第26節的註釋）都有權利吃它們主人丟給它們的「碎渣兒」。這個不平常的婦人準備好要接受基督可能會給她的任何級別的仁慈，甚至於都不爲這點爭論，只要他願意答應她的請求就行了。請比較那麻風病人面對主要障礙時的堅持不懈（見對@可1:40-45@的註釋）。

29.zh:
耶穌離開那地方，來到靠近加利利的海邊，就上山坐下。

**耶穌離開那地方**。[治好一個聾啞人；在低加波利行的其他神蹟，太15:29-31=可7:31-37。主要的註釋在：馬可福音。]

26.zh:
他回答說：「不好拿兒女的餅丟給狗吃。」

**不好**。即，不適合或不適當或不好。基督在這裏表達的是猶太人對外邦人的典型態度，認爲他們不配得上天的祝福。
**餅**。即，救恩的「糧」（見約6:32），就是上帝曾委托給猶太人，他的「兒女」的，爲要將之分發給外邦人，但猶太人却將之私藏了（見《路》第二十三章）。
**狗**。希臘文kunaria，「小狗」，在這裏用來指外邦人（見對@太7:6@的註釋）。猶太人認爲救恩的福份如果給了外邦人就浪費了，照猶太人的觀點看，外邦人沒有能力賞識這些福份或受益於這些福份。基督假裝對那婦人采取輕視的態度可能會使她氣餒，但毋庸置疑，他相信她的信心不會失敗（見林前10:13）。她似乎確信基督能給她心中所想的，只要他願意就可以（見對@可1:40@的註釋）。驕傲和偏見對她來說算不得什麽，她也不讓這些阻止她。她的信心和恒心都確實值得表揚。

23.zh:
耶穌卻一言不答。門徒進前來，求他說：「這婦人在我們後頭喊叫，請打發她走吧。」

**一言不答**。基督的目的是要教導門徒們一個在爲非猶太人作工方面的教訓，他是通過先扮演猶太人通常的態度，再將之與他自己的態度進行對比來施教的（見對第21節的註釋）。典型的猶太拉比會做的與門徒們的提議一樣，對她的請求連一個直接的回答都不給就打發她走。耶穌本人對外邦人的關切，與他們適合享有天國的特權一樣，從他曾論到他們的話中都是顯而易見的（見路4:26,27），加之他在先前的場合對他們所做的事。耶穌决沒有猶太人對外邦人懷有的那種狹隘的排外情緒（見對太15:22,26的註釋）。
**門徒進前來**。他們並不重視由這個外邦婦人熱情洋溢的請求引起的宣傳效應，他們看她不過像一條狗（見對@太10:5@的註釋）。她不僅是一個外人；還是一個女人。不僅如此，她還是一個外國人。在他們的觀念中，還絲毫沒有想到爲陌生的外國女人傳福音的事。

6.en: And honour not. The first sentence of v. 15:6 as it appears in the KJV actually continues and completes the thought of v. 5. Verse 6 would better begin with the words, “Thus have ye made.” Commandment. Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 146) the reading “word.”
6.zh:
他就可以不孝敬父母。’這就是你們藉著遺傳，廢了上帝的誡命。

**不孝敬**。太15:6的第一個句子在欽定本中似乎實際上繼續並完成的是第5節的思想。第6節以「這就是你們」開始會更好。
**誡命**。原文證據支持（參本册註釋原文第146頁）讀作「話」。

15.zh:
耶穌給他們按手，就離開那地方去了。

**按手**。見對@可10:16@的註釋。耶穌的觸摸經常給病人帶來醫治，現在也給了孩子們祝福。值得注意的是，耶穌並沒有給他們施洗，而只是將他們交託給愛他們並照顧著他們的天父。

19.en: Love thy neighbour. This sums up all the “commandments” Jesus here refers to (see on ch. 22:39, 40). Though the young man did not as yet realize it, these precepts of conduct went to the very heart of his problem. He did not love other men as much as he loved himself. Yet he felt he had “kept” “all these things.” He had observed the letter of the law but not its spirit, yet he considered himself to be living in harmony with its principles. Jesus seeks to open the young man’s eyes to the fact that the principles of the law must be conscientiously applied to all the practical relationships of life.
19.zh:
當孝敬父母，又當愛人如己。」

**愛人如己**。耶穌在這裏提到提所有「誡命」的總結（見對@太22:39,40@的註釋）。雖然這個青年人還沒有認識到這一點，但這些行爲準則却正是他的病根。他並沒有像愛他自己那樣愛別人。然而他却感到自己已經「遵守了」「這一切」。他遵守了律法的字句，却沒有遵守律法的精神，然而他却認爲自己的生活與律法的原則是一致的。耶穌尋求打開這個青年人的眼睛，使他看到事實上律法的原則必須本著良心應用於人生所有的實際關係中。

2.zh:
有許多人跟著他，他就在那裏把他們的病人治好了。

**許多人**。與在加利利傳道的最盛時期一樣（見路12:1,14；14:25等）。此時以前耶穌還沒有在比哩亞工作過。這個地區含有相當大的一部分猶太人，而且在當時人口相當稠密。他確實應該照顧那裏人們的需要，就像照顧猶太地和加利利地人們的需要一樣。

24.zh:
我又告訴你們，駱駝穿過針的眼，比財主進上帝的國還容易呢！」

**駱駝**。耶穌說的是人不可能做到的事，正如他所明說的（見第26節）。所說的這個真理正好與人們甚至是門徒們所信的相反（見對第25節的註釋）。法利賽人認爲並且教導說財富乃是蒙上帝喜愛的一個證據（見對@路16:14@的註釋）。當耶穌在這個場合論述財富時，他心裏可能特別想著猶大—猶大應該早日克服愛錢財的心（見約12:6；13:29）。猶太的問題在根本上與那個富足的少年官的問題是一樣的（見對@可3:19@的註釋）。
**針的眼**。認爲「針的眼」指的是在大城門的門板上開的一個小門，當大城門的主要交通關閉時，人還可以從那裏經過，這種解釋起源於基督以後的世紀。所以，這種解釋雖然看似有理，但却沒有有效地根據。耶穌要表達的是不可能做到（第26節），所以想另闢蹊徑，把耶穌明確指出是不可能的事解釋爲有可能的事的是沒有意義的。
**比財主**。見對@路12:15,21@的註釋。與通常擁有財富的人形成了快樂的對比，馬太拋棄了財富以便可以跟從夫子（見對@可2:13,14@的註釋），另一個富有的稅吏長撒該，也將自己的愛情從財富轉向了耶穌（見對路19:2,8的註釋）。

28.zh:
耶穌說：「我實在告訴你們，你們這跟從我的人，到復興的時候，人子坐在他榮耀的寶座上，你們也要坐在十二個寶座上，審判以色列十二個支派。

**實在**。見對@太5:18@的註釋。
**復興**。或，「更新」。在這裏耶穌指的是這個世界的「重建」或「更新」，即，指的是地球處於重新受造的狀態（見賽65:17；彼後3:13；啟21:1）。
**人子**。見對@太1:1@；@可2:10@的註釋。
**他的榮耀的寶座**。或「他榮耀的寶座」（見對@太16:27；25:31@的註釋）。
**十二個寶座**。他們要與耶穌同作王（見提後2:12；啟3:21；20:6）。

9.en: I say unto you. See on ch. 5:22. The only change made to accommodate the original marriage law to a fallen world is that violation of the marriage contract by unchastity may constitute a lawful basis for dissolving the union. Otherwise, the union may not lawfully be broken. Whosoever. The principle Christ is about to state is of universal application. No one who professes to be a Christian should think himself an exception to it. Fornication. Gr. porneia (see on ch. 5:32). It should be noted that in the NT the term “fornication” covers all illicit relationships both before and after marriage. To the modern English reader the word “unchastity” conveys more exactly the meaning of porneia as it is used in the NT. Under the Mosaic law the penalty for marital unfaithfulness was death (see on Lev. 20:10), not divorce. Furthermore, under Moses’ law the death penalty was mandatory, whereas under the Christian law here set forth by Christ divorce is not mandatory, but permissible. From Jesus’ teachings here it may be inferred that the innocent party is free to choose whether the marriage relationship shall be continued. Reconciliation is ever the ideal, especially if children are involved. Here and in Jesus’ parallel discussion in Matt. 5:32 it seems to be implied, even though not specifically stated, that the innocent party to a divorce is at liberty to marry again. This has been the understanding of the great majority of commentators through the years. Marrieth her which is put away. Any alliance she contracts with another man violates her original marriage vow, which violation constitutes adultery. By a parity of reasoning the man marrying her becomes an adulterer also.
9.zh:
我告訴你們，凡休妻另娶的，若不是為淫亂的緣故，就是犯姦淫了；有人娶那被休的婦人，也是犯姦淫了。」

**我告訴你們**。見對@太5:22@的註釋。爲使起初的婚姻律法適應墮落的世界所作的唯一改變，就是由不貞而違背婚約可以構成解散這一結合的法律根據。否則，破壞這一結合就是不合法的。
**凡**。基督即將要說的原則是通用的原則。凡自稱爲基督徒的人無一例外都應遵守。
**淫亂**。希臘文porneia（見對@太5:32@的註釋）。應該注意的是，在新約聖經中，「淫亂」這個詞涵蓋了婚前婚後的所有非法關係。對現代英語的讀者來說，「unchastity」（「不貞」）這個詞更準確地傳達了porneia被用在新約聖經中的意思。在摩西律法之下，對婚姻不忠的刑罰乃是死刑（見對@利20:10@的註釋），而不是離婚。此外，在摩西律法之下，死刑是强制性的，而基督在這裏所提出的基督教律法之下，離婚並不是强制性的，而是可允許的。從耶穌在這裏所講的教訓可以推斷，無辜的一方可以自由選擇是否將婚姻關係繼續下去。和好總是理想的，特別是涉及到孩子的時候。
耶穌在這裏以及在太5:32中所做的類似論述，即使沒有明確地說出來，也似乎暗示離婚中無辜的一方有自由再婚。多年來，約大多數的註釋者們都是這樣理解的。
**娶那被休的婦人**。她與另一個男人的任何聯合都違背了她起初的婚姻誓約，這種違背就構成了奸淫。由此類推，娶她的那個男人也就成了一個奸夫。

13.en: Then. [Blessing the Children, Matt. 19:13–15=Mark 10:13–16=Luke 18:15–17. Major comment: Mark.] The thought sequence is here stressed rather than the immediate time sequence. Were there brought. Jews customarily took their children, particularly at the age of one year, to be blessed by a rabbi (see DA 511): Rebuked them. The disciples completely misunderstood Jesus. They considered this request a waste of their Master’s time and an unnecessary interruption in what was, to them, the more important task of preaching the gospel to adults. They thought they were protecting Jesus from annoyance. According to Mark, Jesus was “much displeased” with the peremptory action of the disciples (see ch. 10:14).
13.zh:
那時，有人帶著小孩子來見耶穌，要耶穌給他們按手禱告，門徒就責備那些人。

**那時**。[爲小孩祝福，太19:13-15=可10:13-16=路18:15-17。主要的註釋在：馬可福音。] 這裏側重於思想順序而不是直接地時間順序。
**有人帶著**。猶太人習慣於把自己的孩子，特別是在孩子一歲的時候，帶到拉比面前受祝福（見《歷》第五十六章）。
**責備那些人**。門徒們完全誤解了耶穌。他們認爲這樣的請求乃是浪費他們夫子的時間，對他們來說，也不必要地打斷了向成人傳福音的更重要的任務。他們以爲自己在保護耶穌免受煩擾。依照馬可福音，耶穌「惱怒」門徒們這種專橫的行爲（見可10:14）。

11.zh:
耶穌說：「這話不是人都能領受的，惟獨賜給誰，誰才能領受。

**不是人都能領受的**。門徒們的意見（第10節）顯出了他們的困惑，導致耶穌作了進一步的講論（第12節）。
**這話**。直譯是，「這個話語」，即，門徒們剛才說的話（第10節），論到耶穌先前講到淫亂和離婚的話（第9節）。
**惟獨**。每個人都必須自由地决定是否將這句話應用於自己的情况。上帝曾親自宣布說：「那人獨居不好」（創2:18），然而在罪的統治下，耶穌在這裏似乎承認有時候會有某些環境對人來說「獨居」更好。

4.en: Have ye not read? See on Mark 2:25. Again, as always, Jesus directs His hearers to the Scriptures, to the “law,” for an authoritative statement of doctrine (see on Mark 7:7– 13). He which made them. That is, man and wife, with particular reference to the first man and wife (see on Gen. 1:27). The Greek here is identical with that of a portion of the LXX of Gen. 1:27. At the beginning. That is, at creation (see Mark 10:6). Jesus takes His inquisitors back beyond the law of Moses, which is in their minds at the moment, to the fundamental principles of marriage as instituted at creation.
4.zh:
耶穌回答說：「那起初造人的，是造男造女，

**你們沒有念過嗎**。見對@可2:25@的註釋。與往常一樣，耶穌再次把他的聽衆指向了聖經，指向了「律法」，作爲教義的權威性陳述（見對@可7:7-13@的註釋）。
**那造人的**。即，男人和妻子，特別指第一個男人和妻子（見對@創1:27@的註釋）。這裏的希臘詞與七十士譯本的創1:27中的那部分相同。
**起初**。即，創造的時候（見可10:6）。耶穌把他的詢問者們從此刻他們心中所想的摩西律法，帶到了很早以前在創造的時候設立的婚姻的基本原則。

14.en: Suffer little children. That is, permit or allow the little children to come. This usage of the word “suffer,” though proper, is now rather infrequent. It is apparent that Jesus loved children and that they loved Him. He appreciated their unaffected love and devotion. He was interested in them and fond of them. Upon more than one occasion He referred to the characteristics and interests of childhood to illustrate spiritual truth (see chs. 11:16, 17; 18:2–4; etc.). Forbid them not. Literally, “do not continue hindering them.” Any who make it difficult for children to find the Master today are sure to encounter His utmost displeasure and to earn His severest rebuke. There is room for little children in the kingdom of divine grace. In the home, in the church, in the school, the needs and interests of children are ever to be accorded a place of major importance. All who have any contact with children, or who may have a voice in decisions that affect their interests, must beware of doing anything that might make it difficult for them to find Jesus. Of such. See on ch. 18:3.
14.zh:
耶穌說：「讓小孩子到我這裏來，不要禁止他們；因為在天國的，正是這樣的人。」

**讓小孩子**。即，准許或允許小孩子們過來。顯然，耶穌愛小孩子們，小孩子們也愛他。他重視他們自然真摯地愛與奉獻。他對他們感興趣並且喜愛他們。他不只在一個場合用孩童時期的特徵和興趣來說明屬靈的真理（見太11:16,17；18:2-4等）。
**不要禁止他們**。直譯是，「不要繼續阻止他們」。現今任何使孩子們難於找到主的行爲，都必定會遭到他的極其不滿意，並招致他最嚴厲的責備。在神聖恩典之國裏有小孩子們的地方。在家裏、在教會、在學校裏，總是要對孩子們的需要和興趣給予主要的關注。凡與孩子們接觸的人，或參與作出影響孩子們利益的决定的人，必須小心，不要做任何可能使他們難於找到耶穌的事。
**正是這樣的人**。見對@太18:3@的註釋。

3.en: The Pharisees. [Marriage and Divorce, Matt. 19:3–12=Mark 10:2–12. Major comment: Matthew. See on Matt. 5:27–32.] Luke 9:51 to 18:14, which is sometimes termed Luke’s “great insertion” (see on Luke 9:51), logically falls between vs. 2 and 3 of Matt. 19. Luke is the only gospel writer to cover the incidents and teachings that he records in chs. 9 to 18, which deal largely with the Peraean ministry. At the time the incident here recorded took place, apparently but a few weeks intervened until the Passover of A.D . 31. Concerning the beliefs and practices of the Pharisees see pp. 51, 52. Tempting him. Or, “testing Him” (see on ch. 4:1), that is, with the purpose of entrapping Him. For nearly two years now spies commissioned by the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem had followed Jesus with the twofold objective of finding some accusation to bring against Him and of attempting to discredit Him in the eyes of the people (see DA 213). Upon two previous occasions since the Feast of Tabernacles (see on ch. 19:1) attempts had been made in Jerusalem to stone Jesus (see John 8:59; 10:31–33). It was commonly known that His life was in danger should He again venture into Judea (see John 11:8), for the Jewish leaders were seeking His arrest (John 11:57). Again and again since the healing of the man at the Pool of Bethesda (see John 5:1–9) the scribes and Pharisees had sought to entrap Jesus with questions calculated to elicit statements that might later be made the basis of charges against Him (see Mark 7:2,5; 8:11; John 8:6; etc.). See on Matt. 16:1. Put away his wife. That is, “divorce” her. See on ch. 5:31. For every cause. For comment see on ch. 5:31, 32.
3.zh:
有法利賽人來試探耶穌，說：「人無論什麼緣故都可以休妻嗎？」

**法利賽人**。[結婚與離婚，太19:3-12=可10:2-12。主要的註釋在：馬太福音。見對@太5:27-32@的註釋。] 路9:51至18:14有時被稱爲路加的「偉大插入」（見對@路9:51@的註釋），邏輯上可以插在馬太福音第19章的第2節和第3節之間。路加是唯一一位涵蓋了主要發生在比哩亞傳道時的事件和教訓的福音書作者，他將之記錄在第9到18章。記載在這裏的事件發生時，顯然距公元31年的逾越節不過幾周的時間。關於法利賽人的信仰和實踐，見本册註釋原文第51,52頁。
**試探耶穌**。或「試驗他」（見對@太4:1@的註釋），即，目的是要誘騙他。近兩年來耶路撒冷的猶太議會所委任的探子們一直跟隨著耶穌，目的是要找到某種罪狀反對他，並企圖在百姓面前誹謗他（見《歷》第二十一章）。自從住棚節以來（見對太19:1的註釋），在耶路撒冷已有兩個場合猶太人要拿石頭打死耶穌（見約8:59；10:31-33）。大家都知道他要是再斗膽進入猶太地，生命就會有危險（見約11:8），因爲猶太領袖們正在尋求逮捕他（約11:57）。自從在畢士大池邊治好那個癱子以來（見約5:1-9），文士和法利賽人三番四次地努力用提問，誘使耶穌說出可以後來作爲根據控告他的話來（見可7:2,5；8:11；約8:6等）。見對@太16:1@的註釋。
**休妻**。即，跟她「離婚」。見對@太5:31@的註釋。
**無論什麽緣故**。關於的註釋，見對@太5:31,32@的註釋。

17.en: Why callest thou me good? Evidently the manner in which the young man addressed Jesus was quite unusual (cf. John 3:2). There seems to be no record in rabbinical literature that rabbis were ever addressed as “good.” On the contrary, in the Mishnah, God Himself is spoken of as “he that is good and bestows good” (Berakoth 9. 2, Soncino ed. of the Talmud, p. 327). The young man’s station in life and his office of public trust (see on Matt. 19:16) indicate that he did not call Jesus “good Master” out of ignorance or carelessness. It was obvious that he had a reason for doing so, and Jesus sought to draw out of him a public statement of that reason. Jesus’ explanation, “there is none good but one” was to help the young man to realize clearly the import of his salutation. Jesus recognized the sincerity and discernment of the young man, and thought to strengthen his faith by drawing out of him an even clearer statement of it. None good but one. Supreme goodness is a characteristic of God alone (Ex. 34:6; Ps. 23:6; 27:13; 31:19; 52:1; Rom. 2:4; etc.). Jesus does not disavow His deity, as might at first appear, but rather clarifies and emphasizes the full significance of the young man’s statement. Enter into life. Equivalent to the expression, “enter into the kingdom of heaven” (see ch. 5:20). In view of the fact that Jesus includes both this life and the life to come in His remarks on the rewards of discipleship (see Matt. 19:29; Mark 10:30; Luke 18:30), it may be appropriate to conclude that both the kingdom of grace and the kingdom of glory are included here. Commandments. Gr. entolai, “precepts,” “orders,” “charges,” or “commands” (cf. on Ps. 19:8). The entolai are the specific, individual requirements, or commands, enjoined upon men by the “law,” Gr. nomos (cf. on Ps. 19:7; Prov. 3:1). It is the will of God that man shall reflect His character, and His character may be summed up in the one word “love” (1 John 4:7–12). To reflect the character, or “love,” of God, we will love Him supremely and our neighbor as ourselves (see on Matt. 22:37, 39). If we inquire as to how we are to express our love to God and our fellow men, God gives us the answer in the Ten Commandments (see Ex. 20:3–17), which Christ explained and exalted (see on Isa. 42:21) in the Sermon on the Mount (see Matt. 5:17–48). All the civil laws of Moses in the OT and the instructions of Christ and the apostles in the NT clarify the divine requirements set forth in the Ten Commandments and apply them to the practical problems of daily living. The young man professed to love God, but the real test of that love, Jesus says, is to be found in the way he treats his fellow men (see 1 John 4:20). “If ye love me,” Jesus says, “keep my commandments” (John 14:15).
17.zh:
耶穌對他說：「你為什麼以善事問我呢？只有一位是善的（有古卷作：你為什麼稱我是良善的？除了上帝以外，沒有一個良善的）。你若要進入永生，就當遵守誡命。」

**你爲什麽稱我是良善的**。顯然，這個青年人對耶穌說的話是十分非同尋常的（參約3:2）。在拉比文獻中，似乎並沒有拉比曾被稱爲「良善」的記錄。相反，在《米示孥》中，上帝自己才被說到是「良善的並且給予良善的」（Berakoth9.2，《他勒目》之宋西諾版，第327頁）。這個青年人的生活狀况和社會公職（見對太19:16的註釋），表明他稱呼耶穌是「良善的夫子」並非出於無知或輕率。他這麽做顯然是有原因的，耶穌想使他當衆說出那個原因。耶穌說明「除了一位之外再沒有良善的」是要幫助這個青年人清楚地認識到他打這個招呼的重要性。耶穌看出了這青年人的真誠和洞察力，想要通過使他更清楚地說出這一點來加强他的信心。
**除了上帝一位之外再沒有良善的**。至善乃是惟有上帝才具有的一種特性（出34:6；詩23:6；27:13；31:19；52:1；羅2:4等）。耶穌並沒有否認自己的神性，乍看起來可能像那樣，而只是澄清並强調了這個青年人所說話語的重要性。
**進入永生**。相當於說：「進入天國」（見太5:20）。鑒於事實上耶穌在他所說關於作門徒所得的獎賞中，既包括了今生也包括了來生（見太19:29；可10:30；路18:30），可以適當地作出結論說，這裏既包括恩典之國也包括榮耀之國。
**誡命**。希臘文entolai，「訓令」，「命令」，「告誡」或「誡命」（參@詩19:8@的註釋）。entolai是「律法」（希臘文nomos，參@詩19:7@；@箴3:1@的註釋）吩咐人去做的明確的、個別的要求或命令。上帝的旨意是要人反映他的品格，而他的品格可以總括爲一個字「愛」（約壹4:7-12）。要反映上帝的品格，或者說「愛」，我們就必須愛他超過一切並且愛人如己（見對@太22:37,39@的註釋）。如果我們詢問應該如何表示我們對上帝和對同胞的愛，上帝給我們的回答就在十誡裏（見出20:3-17），基督在山上寶訓中（見太5:17-48）對十誡作了解釋和提升（見對@賽42:21@的註釋）。舊約聖經摩西書中所有的民事律法，以及新約聖經中基督和使徒們的教導，都闡明了十誡中的神聖要求，並將之應用於日常生活的實際問題。這個青年人自稱愛上帝，但耶穌說，對這種愛的真實試驗乃在於他對待自己同胞的方式（見約壹4:20）。耶穌說：「你們若愛我，就必遵守我的命令」（約14:15）。

27.zh:
彼得就對他說：「看哪，我們已經撇下所有的跟從你，將來我們要得什麼呢？」

**彼得就對他說**。與往常一樣，彼得又出來作門徒們的代言人了（見對@太16:16；17:4@的註釋等）。
**我們已經撇下所有的**。彼得並沒有言過其實（見對@路5:11@的註釋）。門徒們已經滿足了剛才擺在那富足的少年官面前的基本要求（見對太19:21的註釋）。他們已經做了他所不願意去做的。那麽，他們已經在耶穌所說的做完全人的路上了嗎？他們有資格「進入永生」了嗎（第17節）？
**將來我們要得什麽呢**。彼得想的是做門徒的獎賞。將一隻眼轉向指望獎賞方向的這種捨己，决不會博得上天等著要給予忠心傳道之人的那「做的好」的獎勵（見太25:21,23）。

20.en: From my youth. Important textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 146) for the omission of this phrase. The young man sincerely felt that he had “kept” the commandments, all of them, and was not conscious of any imperfection (see DA 519). What lack I yet? Apparently the young man was confident that there was but a step between him and perfection. But though he had diligently obeyed the letter of the law, he still felt that that was not enough. He felt that he lacked something, but what it was he honestly did not know. His life had been one of purity, honesty, and truthfulness. But his attitude toward his fellow men had been essentially a negative one—he had not stolen their goods, he had not borne false witness against them, he had not taken their wives or their lives. True, the letter of the law is negative in form, but its spirit calls for positive action. It is not enough to avoid hating or hurting our fellow men; the gospel calls upon us to love and help them as we love ourselves. This young man lacked the love of God in his heart (see DA 519), without which his observance of “all these things” was of no real value in the sight of Heaven.
20.zh:
那少年人說：「這一切我都遵守了，還缺少什麼呢？」

**從小時**。重要的原文證據所以被引用（參本册註釋原文第146頁）支持省略這個短語。那青年人真誠地認爲自己已經「遵守了」誡命，都遵守了，並沒有意識到任何的不完全（見《歷》第五十七章）。
**還缺少什麽呢**。顯然地，這個青年人自信只差一步就可以達到完全了。但是雖然他曾殷勤地遵守了律法的字句，却仍感到那不是不够的。他感到自己缺少某種東西，但那是什麽他確實不知道。他的生活一直是純潔、誠實、並且真實的。但他對同胞的態度本質上却一直是消極的—他未曾偷過他們的東西，他沒有做過假見證反對他們，他也沒有奪過他們的妻子或性命。確實，律法的字句在形式上是消極的，但其精神却要求積極的行動。避免憎恨或傷害我們的同胞還不够；福音號召我們去愛並幫助他們就像愛我們自己一樣。這個青年人內心缺乏上帝的愛（見《歷》第五十七章），若沒有上帝的愛，在上天看來，他遵守了「這一切」都是沒有真價值的。

16.en: Behold. [The Rich Young Ruler, Matt. 19:16–30=Mark 10:17–31=Luke 18:18– 30. Major comment: Matthew.] This incident seems to have followed closely the blessing of the children (see vs. 13–15). The “ruler” had witnessed the blessing of the children, and this heart-warming expression of love prompted his question (see DA 518). One came. He is usually called “the rich young ruler,” a composite name based on the three synoptic accounts of the incident. According to Matthew he is said to have been “young” (ch. 19:20), and in Luke he is spoken of as a “ruler” who was “very rich” (ch. 18:18, 23). According to his viewpoint he was conscientious and had lived an exemplary life (see on Matt. 19:19). As a “ruler” he occupied a position of responsibility and was a member of the “honored council of the Jews” (see DA 518, 520). Whether this was the local sanhedrin or council of the town in which he lived or the Great Sanhedrin in Jerusalem is not certain (see p. 67). The rich young ruler seems to have accosted Jesus as He was leaving the town (see Mark 10:17). That the young man came “running” reflects youthful eagerness, and that he “kneeled” indicates sincerity (Mark 10:17). His attitude was markedly in contrast with that of the Pharisees, who had recently come “tempting” Jesus (see Matt. 19:3). This incident and the instruction afterward given the disciples (vs. 23–30) teach first, the importance of self-renunciation as a requirement for entrance into the kingdom of heaven (see on Luke 9:61, 62; 14:26–28, 33), and second, the danger of a love for money (see on Matt. 6:19–12; Luke 12:13–21; 16:1–15). Good Master. Literally, “good Teacher” (see on v. 17). What good thing? This question reflects the typical Pharisaical concept of righteousness by works as a passport to “eternal life” (see on v. 17). The rich young ruler had conscientiously performed all the requirements of the law (COL 391), in a formal way at least, and no doubt all those imposed by the rabbis as well, yet was conscious of a lack in his life. He greatly admired Jesus, and seriously considered becoming one of His disciples (DA 518). For the same question propounded by “a certain lawyer” on a previous occasion see on Luke 10:25.
16.zh:
有一個人來見耶穌，說：「夫子（有古卷作：良善的夫子），我該做什麼善事才能得永生？」

**看哪**。[富足的少年官，太19:16-30=可10:17-31=路18:18-30。主要的註釋在：馬太福音。] 這事似乎是緊接著爲小孩子們祝福發生的（見第13-15節）。那個「青年官」曾目睹了孩子們受祝福，耶穌這種感人的愛的表露促使他提出了自己問題（見《歷》第五十七章）。
**有一個人來**。根據三部對觀福音書對這事的記載，他通常被稱爲「富足的少年官」。依照馬太福音，他被說到是一個「少年人」（太19:20），在路加福音中，說到他是一個「很富足」的「官」（路18:18,23）。照他自己的觀點來看，他是盡責的，並且過了一種可做模範的生活（見對太19:19的註釋）。作爲一個「官」，他身居要職，並且是「猶太人所尊敬的議員」（見《歷》第五十七章）。並不確定他是當地猶太議會或本城政務會的議員，還是耶路撒冷大議會的議員（見本册註釋原文第67頁）。
這個富足的少年官似乎是耶穌離城的時候「跑」來對他說話的（見可10:17）。這個青年人「跑」來反映出青年的熱心，而且他「跪」下表明真誠（可10:17）。他的態度明顯地與法利賽人的態度形成了對比，後者最近曾來「試探」耶穌（見太19:3）。
這事以及後來給門徒們的教訓（第23-30節），首先教導的是自我犧牲作爲進入天國的一個必要條件的重要性（見對@路9:61,62；14:26-28,33@的註釋），其次是愛錢財的危險（見對@太6:19-12@；@路12:13-21；16:1-15@的註釋）。
**良善的夫子**。直譯是，「良善的老師」（見對第17節的註釋）。
**作什麽善事**。這個問題反映了典型的靠行爲稱義作爲進入「永生」的護照的法利賽人的觀念（見對第17節的註釋）。這個富足的少年官至少在形式上曾盡責地履行了律法所有的要求（《路》第二十八章），無疑也履行了拉比們的强加的那些規條，然而仍意識到自己生命中有一種缺乏。他極其欽佩耶穌，並且嚴肅地考慮過要成爲他的一個門徒（《歷》第五十七章）。關於「有一個律法師」在以前的場合曾提出的相同的問題，見對@路10:25@的註釋。

12.zh:
因為有生來是閹人，也有被人閹的，並有為天國的緣故自閹的。這話誰能領受就可以領受。」

**有些閹人**。顯然基督在這裏形容的是某些遭受先天性缺陷的人，不應該認爲這樣的人對這種缺陷負有責任。
**被人閹的**。在古代東方，宮庭侍衛實際上總是閹人（太監）。有些閹人顯然結婚了（見對@創37:36@的註釋）。那些閹人是猶太人憐憫的對像（見賽56:3-5）。在身體上有這種毀傷的人不能擔任祭司職分（見利21:20）。在猶大後期的歷史中，曾提到過與宮庭有關的太監（耶29:2），但這些人是猶太人還是外邦人不得而知（見對@斯1:10；2:3@的註釋）。他們中至少有一個人，以伯米勒，是一個古實人（即，埃塞俄比亞人）（見耶38:7）。
**自閹的**。婚姻是值得要的。與另一個人的親密聯合遠比一個人「獨居」更能有效而完全地形成品格。在家庭生活親密的、逐日的關係中，通過軟化征服不可愛的品格特性，並且强化更好的品性比任何可能有的其他方式能有更多的造就。那些因爲某種原因沒有一個家的人，從而就錯過了人生最好的品格訓練學校，無法知道人生深刻的喜樂、悲傷、和良機。
獨身生活並不是一般的、正常的狀態，而且說獨身生活本身自然而然就能比別的生活導致一種更爲聖潔的狀態，乃是魔鬼的一個欺騙。在猶太人中，獨身生活是不受贊成或讓人覺得可憐的，只有某些極端禁欲的團體如愛色尼派才過獨身生活（見本册註釋原文第53頁）。聖經明確記載彼得是已婚的，很可能其他門徒們也是已婚的（見對@可1:30@的註釋）。耶穌從來沒有推薦過獨身生活，無論是向基督徒全體還是向基督教領袖們。獨身生活並不是自然的，不像正常的婚姻生活那樣能有助於發展一種均衡的品格。
我們主的話，如果按字面理解，就會與聖經的整體進程背道而馳。毀損身體的想法是可憎的。似乎應當看這句話與基督在太5:30中的聲明相類似。有些的註釋者在林前7:29保羅所說的話中發現了類似，另見第1,2節。無疑地，基督的這些話應該予以像徵性地理解。
**能領受**。見對第11節的註釋。

21.en: Perfect. See on ch. 5:48. Jesus assumes that the young man really means what he says, or rather, what he implies in the question, “What lack I yet?” Perfection had been his ideal. But, as Paul points out, perfection cannot be achieved by works (see Gal. 2:21; Heb. 7:11). If, therefore, the young man would achieve perfection he must not expect to do so by performing works of merit. He must experience a complete change of heart and life. His mind must be transformed, his objectives changed. Go and sell. In a character otherwise lovable (see Mark 10:21), one serious defect remained—selfishness. Unless the blighting influence of selfishness were removed, the rich young ruler could make no further progress toward perfection. The malady may vary from person to person, and the remedy may therefore vary also. When Peter, Andrew, James, and John were called to follow the Master, He did not ask them to sell their boats and fishing tackle, for the reason that these things did not stand in the way of their following Him. Nevertheless, when called, “they forsook all” in order that they might follow the Master (see on Luke 5:11). Whatever a man loves more than he loves Christ, makes him unworthy of Christ (see on Matt. 10:37, 38). Even the most important earthly responsibilities take second place to following Christ in the pathway of discipleship (see on Luke 9:61, 62). Paul “suffered the loss of all things” in order to “win Christ” (see Phil. 3:7–10). To secure possession of the heavenly treasure or to purchase the pearl of great price (see on Matt. 13:44–46), a man must be ready to sell “all that he hath.” But this, the rich young ruler could not bring himself to do. Here was his cross, but he refused to bear it. That thou hast. Literally, “your belongings.” Treasure in heaven. For comment see on ch. 6:19–21. Jesus confronted the young man with the choice between earthly and heavenly treasure. But the young man wanted both, and upon making the discovery that he could not have both, “went away sorrowful” (ch. 19:22). The painful discovery that he could not serve both God and mammon (see on ch. 6:24) was too much for him. Come and follow me. See on Luke 5:11.
21.zh:
耶穌說：「你若願意作完全人，可去變賣你所有的，分給窮人，就必有財寶在天上；你還要來跟從我。」

**完全**。見對@太5:48@的註釋。耶穌假定這個青年人說的是真的，或者更可說是認爲他在「我還缺少什麽？」這個問題中所含有的意思是真的。做完全人一直是他的理想。但是，就如保羅所指出的，完全是無法靠行爲獲得的（見加2:21；來7:11）。所以，如果這個青年人要達到完全，他就必須不指望靠著行爲的功勞去這麽做。他必須經歷內心和生活的徹底改變。他的心意必須被改變，他的目標也要改變。
**去變賣**。這個青年人品格的其他方面很可愛（見可10:21），但其中却保留著一個嚴重的缺陷—自私自利。如果不除掉自私的不良影響，這個富足的少年官在完全方面就不能取得任何進展。不同的人可能有不同的疾病，所以治療的方法也就不同。當彼得、安得烈、雅各、和約翰蒙召跟從夫子時，他並沒有要求他們賣掉他們的船和漁具，因爲這些東西並不會擋住他們跟從他的道路。然而，當蒙召時，他們就「撇下了所有的」，以便可以跟從夫子（見對@路5:11@的註釋）。
一個人無論愛什麽，如果超過愛基督，就使他不配作基督的門徒（見對@太10:37,38@的註釋）。即使是最重要的屬世責任也要被放在次要位置，以便做門徒跟從基督（見對@路9:61,62@的註釋）。保羅「將萬事都當作有損的」，爲要「得著基督」（見腓3:7-10）。要獲得天上的財寶或者說要買到那重價的珠子（見對@太13:44-46@的註釋），一個人必須準備好變賣「他一切所有的」。但這一點那個青年人做不到。這裏就是他的十字架，但他不肯背起它。
**你所有的**。直譯是，「你的所有物」。
**財寶在天上**。相關的註釋，見對@太6:19-21@的註釋。耶穌使這個青年人面臨在地上財寶和天上財寶之間作出選擇。這個青年人兩者都想要，當他發現不能兼得時，「就憂憂愁愁地走了」（太19:22）。發現不能既侍奉上帝又侍奉瑪門（見對@太6:24@的註釋），這對他來說太痛苦了。
**來跟從我**。見對@路5:11@的註釋。

10.zh:
門徒對耶穌說：「人和妻子既是這樣，倒不如不娶。」

**門徒**。顯然是在耶穌和他的門徒們離開法利賽人進了屋子之後，門徒們才表達了自己對所討論的這個問題的看法（見可10:10）。
**既是這樣**。即，如果婚姻把一個人捆綁的像耶穌剛才所說的那麽嚴格的話。似乎門徒們並沒有清楚地理解耶穌早些時候論到婚姻的話（見太5:31,32；路16:18），因此他們對耶穌剛才給出的解釋深感困惑。
**倒不如不娶**。顯然門徒們的推論是，人性既然如此，又有那麽多丈夫與妻子和不來的情况，乾脆終身不娶不是更好嗎？無疑地，耶穌宣布的標準先是對門徒來說似乎都太高了，有時對現今的基督徒來說也是如此。門徒們所忘記的，也就是現今的基督徒們所忘記的，乃是基督提供了另一個解决婚姻不幸福的方法。依照基督的方案，當夫妻的性情與個性不和時，解决辦法是改變性情、心意、和生活（見對@羅12:2@的註釋），非不是改變配偶。在山上寶訓中清楚地闡明了可以完成這一改變所基於的原則（見對@太5:38-48；6:14,15@的註釋）。如果這些原則被應用於婚姻的困境，它們就會産生出與應用於別的社會關係一樣神奇的效果。夫妻雙方如果都樂於遵從基督在山上寶訓中所制定的原則而行，就沒有什麽婚姻難題是無法令人滿意地解决的。而且只要夫妻雙方中有一方願意去這樣做，即使另一方不願意去做，也往往能達到一種實在不同尋常的婚姻和睦度；許多時候最終的結果都是贏得了不願意去做的一方。這種回報的價值遠遠大於所付出的忍耐與自我犧牲。

18.en: Which? In reply to this question Jesus quotes specifically several of the Ten Commandments dealing with a person’s relationships to his fellow men. No doubt in the sight of men the rich young ruler was honest, but in the sight of God, who reads the heart, he did not truly have the interests of his fellow men at heart (see on vs. 19, 20).
18.zh:
他說：「什麼誡命？」耶穌說：「就是不可殺人；不可姦淫；不可偷盜；不可作假見證；

**什麽誡命**。在回答這個問題時，耶穌明確地引用了十誡中涉及人與其同胞的關係的幾條誡命。無疑地，在人看來，這個富足的少年官是誠實的，但在明白人心的上帝看來，他內心裏並不真正關心自己同胞的利益（見對第19,20節的註釋）。

22.en: Sorrowful. Literally, “sorrowing,” or “grieving.” Great was his disappointment when he realized the sacrifice it involved. The eager joy with which he had run up to Jesus (see on v. 16) turned to gloom and sadness. The price of “eternal life” (v. 16), for which the young man came seeking, was higher than he was willing to pay. Great possessions. His possessions constituted the most important thing in his life. They were his idol, and at this shrine he chose to pour out the adoration and devotion of his heart. It was to free him from the clutches of the god of riches that Jesus proposed that he sell all that he had. This was his only hope of heaven (see DA 520). He had great possessions, but without heavenly wisdom to administer them aright, he would find them to be a curse to him rather than a blessing. Eventually, he would lose even what he had (see on ch. 25:28–30).
22.zh:
那少年人聽見這話，就憂憂愁愁的走了，因為他的產業很多。

**憂憂愁愁**。直譯是，「悲哀」或「憂傷」。當他認識到其中所包含的犧牲時，就大失所望。他跑向耶穌時急切的喜樂（見對第16節的註釋）變成了憂憂愁愁。這個青年人來尋求的「永生」的代價（第16節）高過了他所願意付出的。
**産業很多**。他的産業構成了他生命中最重要的部分。它們成了他的偶像，他選擇將內心的崇拜和奉獻都傾倒在這個神殿裏。耶穌提議要他變賣一切所有的，正是要將他從財神的掌握中釋放出來。這是他進入天國的唯一希望（見《歷》第五十七章）。他的産業很多，但是如果沒有正確管理它們的屬天智慧，他就會發現這些産業將成爲他的咒詛而不是祝福。最終，就連他已經有的也會失去（見對@太25:28-30@的註釋）。

1.zh:
耶穌說完了這些話，就離開加利利，來到猶太的境界約但河外。

**說完了這些話**。[最後離開加利利；撒瑪利亞－比哩亞傳道時期的開始，太19:1,2=可10:1=路9:51-56。主要的註釋在：馬太福音。見「比哩亞早期的傳道」；「基督服務的持續時間，加利利傳道時期的開始，主耶穌的傳道生涯」。] 這是馬太的一個慣用語，用來標記耶穌講道的結束（太7:28；11:1；13:53；26:1）。
**就離開加利利**。顯然是耶穌「退到加利利去」（見對@太4:12@的註釋）的續篇。對觀福音書的作者們略去沒提耶穌在公元30年的住棚節訪問耶路撒冷的事（見對@約7:10@的註釋）。關於這個節期，見對@出23:16@；@利23:2@；@申16:13@的註釋。約翰或多或少廣泛記述了那年的住棚節期間以及緊接在住棚節之後耶穌在耶路撒冷的經歷（約7:2至10:21）。在節期的末日曾有一個要逮捕他的嘗試，但失敗了（約7:32,37,44-53；《歷》第五十章）。第二天「清早」正當他在聖殿裏教訓人時，那個不幸的女人在犯奸淫時被捉拿到他面前（約8:2；《歷》第五十章）。似乎關於「世界的光」的講道與猶太人第一次企圖拿石頭要打耶穌一樣（第59節），也是緊接著這個事件發生的（約8:2,12；參《歷》第五十一章）。「幾個月後」，在修殿節時，他們第二次企圖拿石頭打他（《歷》第五十一章；參約10:22,31,33），又一次企圖逮捕他並終止他的傳道（約10:39,40）。
住棚節結束之後，很可能在接下來的安息日，雖然也可能是修殿節前不久的安息日，耶穌治好了那個生來瞎眼的人（約9:1,7,14），並且發表了約10:1-18關於好牧人的講道（《歷》第五十二章）。在住棚節後，耶穌暫時回到了加利利（《歷》第五十三章），但在修殿節後却退到了比哩亞的事實（約10:39,40），加之治好那個生來就是瞎眼的人似乎緊接在關於「世界的光」的講道之後的事實（約8:12-58），可能暗示治好那個瞎眼的人發生在接下來的安息日（約8:12,59；9:1,5,14）。
在此之前一年半，耶穌曾治好了畢士大池邊的那個癱子，便被强拉到猶太議會之前，於是就從猶太退到了加利利（見對@太4:12@的註釋）。現在他再次離開耶路撒冷去了加利利，因爲祭司和拉比們的仇恨，他就暫時留在那裏（見《歷》第五十三章）。
在八月底，耶穌再次離開加利利，最後一次慢慢地一路前進到耶路撒冷。他曾經迅速而悄然地從加利利啟程去參加住棚節，但現在他的行程却是緩慢的，並且是沿著迂回曲折的路綫行走（約7:10）。在這段時期，他派遣了那七十個人（見對@路10:1-24@的註釋），並且在他們的使命結束後參加了修殿節。這個節期之後，他再次離開了該城，退到了比哩亞，並且開始進行他在比哩亞的傳道（約10:40；《歷》第五十三章）。在修殿節和逾越節之間過去了約有16周還是20周（4個月還是5個月），取决於公元30/31年有12個月還是13個月（見本册註釋原文第255,256頁）。這就是在比哩亞傳道的大約時間（參《歷》第五十三章）。關於撒瑪利亞──比哩亞傳道的事件，見對路9:51至18:34的註釋。
比哩亞傳道時期主要的時間順序問題（見本册註釋原文第190頁），在於確定修殿節的事件（約10:22-42）和那些與拉撒路復活有關的事件（約11:1-57）的正確位置，與路加福音記載的這段時期耶穌傳道的關係（路9:51至18:34）。把修殿節事件放在路加福音第10章和第11章之間的原因，在@路11:1@的註釋中闡明了。把拉撒路復活及其相關事件放在路加福音第17章的第10節和11節之間的原因，在@路17:1,11@的註釋中給出了（見本册註釋原文第199頁；參對@約10:40@的註釋）。
**境界**。見對@太15:22@的註釋。
**約旦河外**。這是一種常見的表達方式，用來指約旦河東的地區，可是有時也指西邊的地區（見對@太4:15@的註釋）。在這裏它指的是比哩亞地區，就是與猶太地隔河相望的地區。當時比哩亞和加利利都在希律安提帕的管轄之下（見對@路3:1@的註釋）。

25.zh:
門徒聽見這話，就希奇得很，說：「這樣誰能得救呢？」

**希奇得很**。門徒們對天國的本質（見對@路4:19@的註釋）以及財富作爲蒙上帝喜愛的一個記號的錯誤觀念（見對@路16:14@的註釋），使他們對這一絕對的聲明大感困惑。
**這樣誰能**。門徒們想，如果聲望、影響、和財富並不是蒙上帝喜愛的證據，那麽那些缺乏這些東西的人就更沒有機會了。

30.zh:
然而，有許多在前的，將要在後；在後的，將要在前。」

**在前的，將要在後**。見對@路13:30@的註釋。許多人像那個富足的少年官一樣，外表怎麽看都是先進天國的人，實際却是最後的。太19:30在這事和第23-29節中所記載的後來的討論，以及記載在第20章的在葡萄園中作工的比喻之間，形成了一個連接鏈環。請注意在那個比喻的結尾重複了同樣的總結性聲明（見第16節），耶穌講那個比喻，明確地說明了基督教信仰的這個偉大的逆論。
這事之後幾周—他最後那天在聖殿裏教訓人的時候—耶穌向祭司長和長老們宣布了稅吏和妓女們會比他們先進入天國（太21:31,32）。實際上，從全地都會有許多謙卑、忠心的人配「在上帝的國裏坐席」（路13:29），而以色列的宗教領袖們自己却被「趕到外面」（第28節）。關於在來生顛倒過來的狀况的進一步的論述，請比較財主與拉撒路的比喻（見對@路16:19-31@的註釋）。屬世的成功及衆望所基於的標準完全不同於上帝藉以評價一個人的價值標準。

5.en: For this cause. This quotation, from Gen. 2:24, is almost identical with the text of the LXX. In Genesis the words here quoted appear to be Adam’s statement at the time Eve became his wife, but Jesus specifically assigns to God the statement here cited. Leave father and mother. During childhood and youth a person’s primary responsibility is to his father and mother. This responsibility continues throughout life (see on Mark 7:11). However, notwithstanding the importance of this obligation it is subordinate to the marriage law, and where the two may come into conflict—as the result of human weaknesses and mistakes—a man’s first responsibility is to his wife. One flesh. The more a man and woman have in common even before marriage, the greater likelihood that they have will find the companionship marriage should bring and that the union will be a complete success. Conversely, where there are great differences in background, training, attitudes, principles, likes, and dislikes, it is far more difficult to be “one” in mind and spirit, and thus to find success in the marriage relationship.
5.zh:
並且說：‘因此，人要離開父母，與妻子連合，二人成為一體。’這經你們沒有念過嗎？

**因此**。這節經文引自創2:24，幾乎與七十士譯本的原文一字不差。在創世記中，這裏引用的話乃是當夏娃成爲亞當的妻子時亞當所說的話，但耶穌明確地把這裏所引用的話歸給了上帝。
**離開父母**。在童年和青年時期，一個人主要對自己的父親和母親負責。這一責任是持續終身的（見對@可7:11@的註釋）。然而，儘管這個義務很重要，還是從屬於婚姻律法的，當這兩種責任産生衝突時—因爲人類的軟弱和錯誤引起的—人首先要對自己的妻子負責。
**一體**。一個男人和一個女人在結婚前的共同點越多，他們就越可能會發現婚姻應該帶來伴侶關係，而且他們的結合會圓滿成功。相反地，兩個人的背景、訓練、態度、原則、喜好、和嫌惡的差別越大，就越難在心智和精神上成爲「一體」，因而就難於在婚姻關係中得到成功。

7.en: Why did Moses? See Deut. 24:1–4. Divorcement. See on Deut. 24:4; Matt. 5:31. Put her away. See on ch. 5:31.
7.zh:
法利賽人說：「這樣，摩西為什麼吩咐給妻子休書，就可以休她呢？」

**摩西爲什麽**。見申24:1-4。
**休書**。見對@申24:4@；@太5:31@的註釋。
**休她**。見對@太5:31@的註釋。

29.en: Forsaken houses. The disciples had forsaken house and family that they might follow Jesus (see on Luke 5:11), not in the sense of leaving their families destitute, but rather in the sense of making the service of Christ their primary objective. Shortly before Jesus had stated this requirement of discipleship in even stronger terms (see on Luke 14:26). For my name’s sake. See on ch. 5:11. An hundredfold. Compare Job 42:10; Luke 18:30. Jesus is obviously speaking in figurative language. Approximately a year and a half before this, Jesus had observed that those who do the will of His Father in heaven are His “mother” and “sister” and “brother” (see Matt. 12:46–50). The “hundredfold” that Christians receive in this life consists in the joy of Christian fellowship and in the more real and intense satisfaction that comes with service for God. Paul speaks of “having nothing, and yet possessing all things” (2 Cor. 6:10). Everlasting life. See on John 3:16; 6:27. When a man gives up all to follow Christ, he receives in return “a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory” (2 Cor. 4:17). Similarly, this was what Jesus had done in order to make the plan of salvation possible (Phil. 2:6–8).
29.zh:
凡為我的名撇下房屋，或是弟兄、姐妹、父親、母親、（有古卷添：妻子）兒女、田地的，必要得著百倍，並且承受永生。

**撇下房屋**。門徒們已經撇下了房屋和家庭，以便可以跟從耶穌（見對@路5:11@的註釋），不是在留下他們的家屬受窮乏的意義上，而是在使服侍基督成爲他們的首要目標的意義上。不久之前，耶穌曾用更爲强烈的措辭說過作門徒的這個必要條件（見對@路14:26@的註釋）。
**爲我的名**。見對@太5:11@的註釋。
**百倍**。請比較伯42:10；路18:30。耶穌顯然是用比喻性的語言說的。大約距此一年半以前，耶穌曾說過那些遵行他天父旨意的人就是他的「母親」、「姐妹」、和「弟兄」了（見太12:46-50）。基督徒們在今生得的「百倍」，乃在於基督徒友誼中的喜樂，以及從服侍上帝而來的更爲真實强烈的滿足。保羅說到「似乎一無所有，却是樣樣都有的」（林後6:10）。
**永生**。見對@約3:16；6:27@的註釋。當一個人離棄一切跟從基督時，作爲報答，他就得到了「極重無比永遠的榮耀」（林後4:17）。同樣地，這乃是耶穌爲了使救贖計劃成爲可能所完成的（腓2:6-8）。

26.zh:
耶穌看著他們，說：「在人這是不能的，在上帝凡事都能。」

**看著他們**。即，耶穌很可能觀察到了門徒們臉上驚奇的表情。
**這是不能的**。「在人」是不可能的──但「在上帝」却不然。財主基於人的努力進天國是不可能的，因爲他沒有辦法使自己脫離愛財富之心的魔掌。因爲那個問題，任何人基於自己的努力都不可能得救。要想救財主脫離愛財的心，或救任何一個人脫離脫離纏累他的罪，只有靠神聖恩典的奇迹才能實現（參來12:1）。
**凡事都能**。即，對一個願意讓上帝控制其生命的人來說（見腓4:13）。惟有上帝的能力運行在人的生命中才能帶來品格的改變，滿足進入天國的要求。

23.zh:
耶穌對門徒說：「我實在告訴你們，財主進天國是難的。

**對門徒說**。那個青年人轉身走了，耶穌和他的門徒們繼續行路。
**財主**。見對@太13:7@的註釋。財主進天國是難的，這並不是因爲他的富有，而是因爲他對財富的態度（見對@路12:15,21@的註釋）。亞伯拉罕「極富」（創13:2），但同時却是「上帝的朋友」（雅2:23）。對這個富足的青年官來說，耶穌給他指出的使他可以「進入永生」（太19:17）的「門」太窄了，他從此必須走的「路」太「小」了（見對@太7:13,14@的註釋）。門徒們在這裏有一個機會目睹一個心思專注在財富上的人「進天國」是多麽的難。那在其他方面是正直的，却被撒但成功地捆綁在今世財富的網羅中的人有多少啊！
**天國**。見對@太3:2；4:17；5:2@；@路4:19@的註釋。

8.en: Hardness of your hearts. See on Deut. 14:26. Suffered you. According to Christ’s statement the OT law that made provision for divorce was a concession designed to meet circumstances that were far from ideal (see on Deut. 24:4). However, Christ’s teaching here makes it clear that the provisions of Moses’ law with respect to divorce are quite invalid for Christians (see on Matt. 19:9). From the beginning. The law of Gen. 1:27; 2:24 preceded the law of Deut. 24:1–4 and is superior to it, for in the Eden period of Genesis, God’s ideal for His human children is set forth. God has never repealed the law of marriage He enunciated in the beginning. It was not God’s plan that divorce should ever be necessary. Therefore Christians today who desire and purpose in their hearts to follow God’s plan will not, without scriptural grounds, resort to divorce as a solution to marital difficulties (see on Matt. 19:9).
8.zh:
耶穌說：「摩西因為你們的心硬，所以許你們休妻，但起初並不是這樣。

**你們的心硬**。見對@申14:26@的註釋。
**許你們**。根據基督的話，舊約律法爲離婚所做的規定乃是一個讓步，原意是要對付遠沒有達到理想的境况（見對@申24:4@的註釋）。然而，基督此時的教訓說明，摩西律法有關離婚的規定對基督徒完全無效（見對太19:9的註釋）。
**起初**。創1:27；2:24的律法先於申24:1-4的律法並且比後者優越，因爲在創世時期的伊甸園中，上帝就宣布了適合於他人類兒女的理想。上帝從未廢除他在起初宣布的婚姻律法。上帝並沒有計劃離婚應該在任何時候成爲必要。所以現今願意並决心遵循上帝的計劃的基督徒既沒有聖經根據，就不可訴諸於離婚作爲解决婚姻難題的辦法（見對太19:9的註釋）。

6.en: Wherefore. Jesus here proceeds to state the conclusion to be drawn from the fundamental principle of the marriage relationship cited from Gen. 2:24. No more twain. In the sight of God, husband and wife are one entity, and therefore should be no more divisible than one human body is. What. That is, the new union formed at marriage (v. 5). God hath joined. The marriage relationship was instituted by God, sanctified by God. It was an All-wise Creator who provided for the marriage relationship; it is He who made it possible and desirable. All who enter upon the marriage relationship are therefore “joined,” according to the original plan of God, for life. Let not man put asunder. With the single exception for which Jesus makes provision (see on v. 9), divorce cannot be honored or recognized in heaven. In the sight of God any alliance either of them may enter into with another woman or man, as the case may be, is branded by Christ as adultery.
6.zh:
既然如此，夫妻不再是兩個人，乃是一體的了。所以，上帝配合的，人不可分開。」

**既然如此**。耶穌在這裏進而說出了從引自創2:24的婚姻關係的基本原則得出的結論。
**不再是兩個人**。在上帝看來，丈夫和妻子乃是一個實體，所以像人的身體一樣不可再分開。
**所**。即，在結婚時形成的新結合（第5節）。
**上帝配合的**。婚姻關係乃是上帝所設立、所批准的。那規定了婚姻關係的乃是一位全智的創造主；他使婚姻關係成爲可能和可喜悅的。所以凡進入婚姻關係的人就是按照上帝起初爲生命制定的計劃「配合」的。
**人不可分開**。除了耶穌規定的一個例外（見對第9節的註釋），離婚是無法被天庭尊敬或承認的。在上帝看來，夫妻中任何一方可能與另一個女人或男人的任何結合，看情况，都被基督打上犯奸淫的烙印。

15.en: The death of Herod. He died soon after his slaughter of the infants of Bethlehem (DA 66), 4 B.C. (see pp. 42, 241), of a most painful and loathsome disease. Might be fulfilled. The quotation as here given is from the Hebrew text of Hosea 11:1. The LXX reads, “Out of Egypt I called his children.” In their original setting in Hosea the words of this prophecy refer to the deliverance of the Hebrew people from Egypt. When calling upon Pharaoh to release them, Moses said, “Thus saith the Lord, Israel is my son, even my firstborn” (Ex. 4:22). For Matthew’s application of the words of Hosea 11:1 to Christ see on Deut. 18:15.
15.zh:
住在那裏，直到希律死了。這是要應驗主藉先知所說的話，說：「我從埃及召出我的兒子來。」

**希律死了**。他在屠殺伯利恒嬰孩之後不久就死了（《歷》第六章），在公元前4年（見本册註釋原文第42,241頁），死於最痛苦、最令人討厭的疾病。
**要應驗**。這裏所引用的經文來自何11:1的希伯來原文。七十士譯本讀作：「我從埃及召出他的兒女來」。在最初的背景中，何西阿這句預言指的是希伯來人被救出埃及。當摩西拜訪法老要他釋放以色列人時，曾說：「耶和華這樣說：以色列是我的兒子，我的長子」（出4:22）。關於馬太將何11:1的話用到基督身上，見對@申18:15@的註釋。

19.en: When Herod was dead. [Return to Nazareth, Matt. 2:19–23=Luke 2:39, 40. Mayor comment: Matthew and Luke; see Childhood and Youth of Jesus ; charts, The Reigns of the Herods, Palestine Under the Herodians.] See p. 42.
19.zh:
希律死了以後，有主的使者在埃及向約瑟夢中顯現，說：

**希律死了以後**。[重返拿撒勒，太2:19-23=路2:39,40。主要的註釋在：馬太福音和路加福音；見「耶穌的童年與青年時代」圖表，「希律諸王的統治」，「希律家庭統治下的巴勒斯坦」] 見本册註釋原文第42頁。

2.en: Born King of the Jews. The question implies that the wise men were not Jews; otherwise they would have said “our king.” It seems to have been generally recognized that the savior-king expected by the nations round about was to arise in Judea (see on v. 1). Upon entering Jerusalem, the wise men first made their way to the Temple, over which the star had faded from sight, but in its sacred precincts they found only ignorance, surprise, fear, and contempt (DA 60, 61). His star. Neither a conjunction of planets, as some have thought, nor a nova, as others have suggested. The “star” that appeared on the night of Christ’s birth was a “distant company of shining angels” (DA 60; v. 7). The wise men were led to interpret this unusual phenomenon as the fulfillment of Balaam’s prophecy of “a Star out of Jacob” (Num. 24:17; see DA 60). 2 Nichol, F. D. (1978). The Seventh-day Adventist Bible Commentary : The Holy Bible with exegetical and expository comment. Commentary Reference Series (Mt 1:1). Washington, D.C.: Review and Herald Publishing Association. East. Gr. anatolē, literally, “rising.” The word translated “east” in v. 1 is anatolai, plural of anatolē. Also, in the Greek, anatole– has the definite article, whereas anatolai has not. This difference between the two expressions has led some to the conclusion that in v. 2 Matthew is not referring to the east either as the direction in the sky in which the star appeared or as the designation of the country from which the wise men came, but rather uses anatolē in its literal meaning, “rising.” The clause may be translated “for we have seen his star in [its] rising,” that is, when it first appeared. This proved to be the point in their story that most interested Herod (v. 7). The other interpretation, “for we have seen his star in the east country” is, of course, also possible.
2.zh:
「那生下來作猶太人之王的在哪里？我們在東方看見他的星，特來拜他。」

**那生下來作猶太人之王的在哪里**。這個問題暗示博士們不是猶太人，否則他們就會說「我們的王」了。似乎一般都公認，周圍列國所期盼的，那爲王的救世主要在猶大出現（見對第1節的註釋）。博士們進入耶路撒冷後，首先到了聖殿，那顆星就是在聖殿上方不見的，但是他們在殿的聖地發現的却只是無知、驚奇、恐懼和輕蔑（《歷》第六章）。
**他的星**。既不像有些人所認爲的是行星的會合，也不像有些人提出的是一顆新星。出現在基督降生之夜的那顆「星」乃是「遠遠的一群光明的天使」（《歷》第六章；第7節）。博士們蒙引導解釋這一不同尋常的現像乃是應驗了「有星要出於雅各」的預言（民24:17；見《歷》第六章）。
**東方**。希臘文是anatolē，直譯是，「上升」。在第1節中被譯爲「東方」的詞anatolai，乃是anatolē的複數形式。而且在希臘原文中，anatolē有定冠詞，但anatolai却沒有。這兩種措詞的不同點使得有些人得出結論說：在第2節中，馬太提到的東方既不是指那星出現在空中的方向，也不是指博士們所來自的國家，而是指anatolē這個詞的字面意思：「上升」。該句子可以譯爲：「因爲我們看見他的星上升」，即，在它初次出現的時候。後來證明，在他們的故事中，希律最感興趣的就是這點（第7節）。當然，另一種譯法也是可能的：「因爲我們在東方看見了他的星」。

9.en: Went before them. Setting out from Jerusalem at twilight, in keeping with their custom of traveling at night (see on v. 1), the wise men found their faith renewed by the reappearance of the star.
9.zh:
他們聽見王的話就去了。在東方所看見的那星忽然在他們前頭行，直行到小孩子的地方，就在上頭停住了。

**在他們前頭行**。照著他們夜晚旅行的習慣（見對第1節的註釋），博士們黎明時分就從耶路撒冷啟程了，由於那星的再現，他們發現自己的信心也得到了更新。

13.en: A dream. [Flight to Egypt, Matt. 2:13–18. See Childhood and Youth of Jesus; a Synopsis of the Life of Christ] The manner in which the angel had first appeared to Joseph (ch. 1:20). Flee into Egypt. Egypt was now a Roman province, and thus beyond the jurisdiction of Herod. The traditional border of Egypt was the so-called River of Egypt, the Wâdī el– ‘Arîsh, some 100 mi. (160 km.) southwest of Bethlehem. Great numbers of Jews lived in Egypt at this time, and Joseph would not therefore find himself completely among strangers. There were synagogues in the cities, and at one time, even a Jewish temple. Heliopolis (On, cf. Gen. 41:45, 50; Gen. 46:20) is the traditional place where Joseph and Mary fled for safety.
13.zh:
他們去後，有主的使者向約瑟夢中顯現，說：「起來！帶著小孩子同他母親逃往埃及，住在那裏，等我吩咐你；因為希律必尋找小孩子，要除滅他。」

**夢中**。[逃往埃及，太2:13-18。見「耶穌的童年與青年時代」、「基督生平梗概」] 天使初次向約瑟顯現時就是用的這種方式（太1:20）。
**逃往埃及**。埃及當時是羅馬的一個省，所以就超出了希律管轄的權限。埃及傳統的邊界就是所謂的埃及河，阿裏殊河（Wâdī el-`Arîsh），在伯利恒西南約100英里（160千米）。當時有大量的猶太人住在埃及，所以約瑟不會發現自己完全處身在陌生人中。在埃及各城都有會堂，一度還有猶太神殿。傳統上認爲紇流坡利（安城，參創41:45,50；創46:20）乃是約瑟和馬利亞爲安全起見所逃往的地方。

11.en: The house. By this time Jesus was at least 40 days old, perhaps older (see on Luke 2:22). Fell down. A common Oriental manner of expressing supreme respect and reverence, to men, to idols, and to God (see Esther 8:3; Job 1:20; Isa. 46:6; Dan. 3:7; etc.). Worshipped him. In spite of their earlier disappointments the wise men knew that this Child was the One for whom they had journeyed far. Their treasures. Gr. thēsauroi, meaning either “caskets,” “treasure chests” used as receptacles for valuables, or “treasures.” The word is translated “treasures” in Matt. 6:20 and in Col. 2:3. The singular (thēsauros) denotes a storehouse in Matt. 13:52. Gifts. In Oriental lands one would never think of paying a visit to a prince or any high official without presenting a gift as an act of homage. Compare the presentation of gifts to Joseph in Egypt (Gen. 43:11), to Samuel (1 Sam. 9:7, 8), to Solomon (1 Kings 10:2), and to God (Ps. 96:8). Frankincense. A white or pale yellow resinous gum obtained by making incisions in the bark of trees of the genus Boswellia. It is bitter to the taste but fragrant when burned as incense. It was used as an ingredient in the sacred incense for the sanctuary (Ex. 30:8, 34). It was usually imported from Arabia (Isa. 60:6; Jer. 6:20). Myrrh. Another aromatic gum highly prized in ancient times, bitter and slightly pungent in taste. It was probably obtained from a small tree, the Balsamodendron myrrha or Commiflora myrrha, native to Arabia and East Africa. It was an ingredient used in compounding the holy oil (Ex. 30:23–25), and perfume (Esther 2:12; Ps. 45:8; Prov. 7:17), and was used as an anodyne, mixed with wine (Mark 15:23), and for embalming (John 19:39).
11.zh:
進了房子，看見小孩子和他母親馬利亞，就俯伏拜那小孩子，揭開寶盒，拿黃金、乳香、沒藥為禮物獻給他。

**房子**。到現在，耶穌至少已經降生40天了，可能更久些（見對@路2:22@的註釋）。
**俯伏**。這是一個常見的東方禮貌，表示對人、對偶像、以及對上帝極度的尊重和崇敬（見斯8:3；伯1:20；賽46:6；但3:7等）。
**拜他**。博士們儘管早先曾經歷失望，但他們知道這個孩子就是他們千里迢迢來尋求的一位。
**寶盒**。希臘文是thēsauroi，意思是用來裝貴重物品的「首飾盒」，「百寶箱」，或者「珍寶」。這個詞在太6:20中被譯爲「財寶」，在西2:3中被譯爲「積蓄」。其單數形式（thēsauros）在太13:52中表示庫房。
**禮物**。在東方國家，若不呈上表示敬意的禮物，就不要想去覲見君王或任何一位高官。請比較獻禮物給在埃及的約瑟（創43:11），給撒母耳（撒上9:7,8），給羅所門（王上10:2），以及給上帝（詩96:8）。
**乳香**。一種白色或淺黃色樹脂膠，通過割開Boswellia類的樹皮可以獲得。它味苦，但當作香點燃時却很芳香。在聖所的崇祀中，它被用作聖香的一種成分（出30:8,34）。乳香通常是從阿拉伯半島進口的（賽60:6；耶6:20）。
**沒藥**。另一種芬芳的樹脂，在古時備受贊譽，味苦並且略微有點辛辣。很可能是從一種小樹上獲得的，就是Balsamodendron myrrha或者Commiflora myrrha，原産阿拉伯半島和東非。它是合成聖油（出30:23-25）和香料（斯2:12；詩45:8；箴7:17）的一種成分，並且與酒調和被用作鎮痛劑（可15:23），也用於防腐（約19:39）。

4.en: The chief priests. Probably the officiating high priest and living priests who had formerly held that office, all having been appointed and later deposed by Herod himself. During his reign of about 33 years Herod appointed altogether nine high priests to this sacred office, which was originally intended to be hereditary and for life (Ex. 28:1; 40:12–15; Lev. 21:16–23; Num. 16:40; 17; Num. 18:1–8; Deut. 10:6). Simon, son of Boethus, may have been high priest at this time (Josephus Antiquities xv. 9. 3), or Matthias or Joazar, son-in-law and son of Boethus, respectively, who followed Simon in rapid succession (ibid., xvii. 4. 2; 6. 4; 13. 1). Others have suggested that the “chief priests” were heads of the 24 courses (see on Luke 1:5). The group Herod summoned seems to have been the learned men of the nation, who would be most likely to have the information he desired. Scribes. These men are often spoken of as lawyers (Matt. 22:35; Mark 12:28), or “doctors of the law,” literally, “teachers of the law” (Luke 5:17, 21). They were learned men whose duty it was to study, preserve, copy, interpret, and expound the Law, or sacred writings (see p. 55; see on Mark 1:22). Demanded. Or, “inquired,” the form of the verb, in Greek, implying that Herod inquired persistently. The priests apparently evaded a direct answer. Herod had to draw it out of them. The wise men had probably referred to their study of the Hebrew Scriptures, and if so, Herod could rightly have surmised that the doctors of the law must have known more than they appeared to. They were by no means as ignorant as they pretended to be, either of the prophecies themselves or of recent events that pointed to their fulfillment. They knew, no doubt, of the vision of Zacharias (Luke 1:22), of the report of the shepherds (see on Luke 2:17), and of the prophecy of Simeon (Luke 2:27, 28, 34, 35). But pride and envy closed the door of their hearts to light, for obviously God had passed them by in favor of uncouth shepherds and uncircumcised heathen, as they thought. They branded the reports as fanaticism and unworthy of attention (see DA 62, 63). Where Christ should be born. Here Herod seeks to ascertain the place of Christ’s birth, as later, from the wise men, the time (v. 7).
4.zh:
他就召齊了祭司長和民間的文士，問他們說：「基督當生在何處？」

**祭司長**。很可能是擔任大祭司職分的人和從前曾擔任過那職分的現任祭司們，都是被指定的，後來被希律廢除了。在希律統治的33年中，他總共指定了九位大祭司擔任這神聖的職責，這職責起初本是規定爲世襲的，並且是終身的（出28:1；40:12-15；利21:16-23；民16:40；17；民18:1-8；申10:6）。伯修的兒子西門，可能是那時的大祭司（約瑟夫，《猶太掌故》，xv.9.3），要不就是伯修的女婿馬提亞或者伯修的兒子約阿撒，他們都迅速地作了西門的繼任者（同上，xvii，4.2；6.4；13.1）。還有人提出說「祭司長們」是按著24個班次供職的祭司們的首領（見對@路1:5@的註釋）。希律所召集的這群人似乎是該國有學問的人士，他們最有可能知道他想得到的消息。
**文士**。這些人經常被說成是律法師（太22:35；可12:28），或者「律法的博士」，直譯是「教法師」（路5:17,21）。他們是有學問的人，其責任是研究、保存、抄寫、解釋並詳細說明律法，或神聖的著作（見本册註釋原文第55頁；見對@可1:22@的註釋）。
**問**。或「詢問」這個詞在希臘原文中的詞形暗示希律堅持不懈地詢問。祭司們顯然規避直接答覆。希律就不得不逼他們說出來了。博士們很可能提到了自己對希伯來聖經的研究，假如這樣的話，希律就能正當地猜想律法師們肯定深藏不露。不管是對於這些預言本身，還是對近來要應驗這些預言的事件，他們决不像他們假裝的那樣無知、無疑。他們知道撒迦利亞的異像（路1:22），知道牧羊人的報告（見對@路2:17@的註釋），也知道西面的預言（路2:27,28,34,35）。但是驕傲和嫉妒關閉了他們的心門，不接受亮光，因爲上帝既然支持他們所認爲粗俗的牧羊人和未受割禮的外邦人，就顯然已經越過了他們。他們就誣衊這報告是狂熱盲信，不值得注意（見《歷》第六章）。
**基督當生在何處**。希律在這裏尋求探知基督降生的地點，像他後來向博士們打探基督降生的時間一樣（第7節）。

14.en: By night. Joseph doubtless obeyed without delay, probably leaving the same night or as soon thereafter as preparations could be made for the journey. The gifts presented by the wise men provided the necessary means for the journey (DA 65).
14.zh:
約瑟就起來，夜間帶著小孩子和他母親往埃及去，

**夜間**。約瑟無疑毫不遲疑地順從了，很可能當晚就離開了，或者一作好這次旅行的準備就啟程了。博士們獻上的禮物提供了這次行程所必須的費用（《歷》第六章）。

3.en: He was troubled. The catalogue of atrocities by Herod, particularly the murder of various members of his immediate family whom he suspected of plotting to do away with him and usurp his throne, testifies eloquently to the feelings of his heart upon hearing that One destined to be “King of the Jews” had been born (see pp. 61, 62). The seeming reticence of the priests to divulge information concerning the Messianic prophecies, which the wise men had no doubt mentioned, led Herod to suspect the priests of conniving with the wise men in a plot to unseat him from his throne, perhaps by exciting a popular tumult. Furthermore, it is probable that Herod himself knew of the popular expectation that a prince was to be born in Judea who was destined to rule the world. Not only so; he appears to have regarded himself as the Messiah and to have had secret longings to rule the world (see Joseph Klausner, The Messianic Idea in Israel, p. 374). All Jerusalem. It is little wonder the whole city was “troubled” also, because its residents were too familiar with the atrocities of which Herod was capable. Fearing a popular tumult, he might well decree the slaughter of hundreds or thousands of the people.
3.zh:
希律王聽見了，就心裏不安；耶路撒冷合城的人也都不安。

**希律心裏不安**。希律所犯下的累累殘暴的惡行，特別是謀殺了許多他懷疑圖謀廢除他和篡奪他寶座的直系親屬的暴行，有力地證明了當他聽到那注定要作「猶太人之王」的一位已經降生時的感受（見本册註釋原文第61,62頁）。祭司們對公布關於彌賽亞的預言，就是博士們肯定提到過的預言所表現的冷淡態度，使希律懷疑祭司們與這些博士暗中圖謀推翻他的寶座，有可能會藉著發動一次公衆的暴亂進行。而且，可能希律自己也知道大衆期待一位王在猶大降生，乃是注定要統治全世界的。不僅如此；他似乎已經把自己當作彌賽亞了，並且背地裏渴望統治全世界（見約瑟夫·克勞斯[Joseph Klausner]，《以色列中的彌賽亞觀》[The Messianic Idea in Israel]，第374頁）。
**耶路撒冷合城的人**。合城的人也都「不安」，這一點兒也不奇怪，因爲該城的居民太瞭解希律會采取的暴行了。如果擔心會有一次公開的暴亂，他就很有可能頒布屠殺數百或數千人的命令。

17.en: Then was fulfilled. See Jer. 31:15. For the original application of this prophecy see on Jer. 31:15, and for the Messianic application see on Deut. 18:15.
17.zh:
這就應了先知耶利米的話，說：

**這就應了**。見耶31:15。關於這個預言最初的應用，見對@耶31:15@的註釋，關於彌賽亞的應用，見對@申18:15@的註釋。

20.en: Land of Israel. A general term denoting all of Palestine. They are dead. Some think the plural refers to Herod and his son and heir apparent, Antipater (slain a short time prior to Herod’s death); others, that it includes the soldiers who participated in the massacre of the infants of Bethlehem.
20.zh:
「起來！帶著小孩子和他母親往以色列地去，因為要害小孩子性命的人已經死了。」

**以色列地**。指全巴勒斯坦的一個通稱。
**他們已經死了**。有些人認爲複數代詞指的是希律和他兒子及有確定繼承權的人，安提帕特（在希律死前不久被殺）；有些人認爲包括參與屠殺伯利恒嬰孩的士兵們。

16.en: Mocked. They had “tricked” him. He felt that they had outwitted him and made a fool of him. Herod took this as an insult, and doubtless as further proof of a deep and dark plot against him. Slew all the children. Probably only the male children. Critics of the accuracy of the Bible record observe that Josephus, in his lengthy record of atrocities committed by Herod, makes no mention of the slaughter of the infants of Bethlehem. It has been estimated, however, that in a small town whose population was probably no more than about 2,000, including its surrounding districts, there would have been only about 50 or 60 children of the age indicated, and only half that many males. Some estimate the number slightly higher. Josephus might have considered the incident relatively minor when compared with the long catalogue of more heinous crimes of Herod that he does mention. A deed such as this accords well with the callous character of Herod. It was one of the last acts of his life (DA 66). Furthermore, should Josephus mention this evil deed he would be expected to account for it, as he does at length with similar events he does record. This might involve a discussion of the Messianic claims of Jesus of Nazareth, a subject which, as a Jews, he might choose to avoid. And, inasmuch as he was writing an apology of Judaism for the Romans, particularly for the emperor Vespasian, he would avoid mentioning anything that might antagonize Rome. See pp. 75, 76, 94. Coasts. Literally, “borders,” hence, “regions.” In Old English, “coast” meant “frontier,” or “border.” Two years old. According to Oriental reckoning, which still survives in some areas, a child is called “one year old” in its first calendar year, that is, between its birth and the next New Year’s Day; and “two years old” in its second calendar year—even if it had lived only a few days or weeks. If the Jews of Christ’s time counted age thus, by calendar years, it is not necessary to suppose that He was born two years before Herod died, or even that Herod, in order to make sure of his objective, set the “two-year” age limit beyond the time indicated by the wise men (Matt. 2:7). A child born at any time in 5/4 B.C. would be “two years old” in 4/3 B.C., the year of Herod’s death. As to the probable time of Jesus’ birth, see pp. 240-242.
16.zh:
希律見自己被博士愚弄，就大大發怒，差人將伯利恒城裏並四境所有的男孩，照著他向博士仔細查問的時候，凡兩歲以裏的，都殺盡了。

**愚弄**。他們已經「捉弄了」他。他感到他們瞞騙嘲弄了他。希律認爲這是一次侮辱，無疑進一步證明了更深更陰暗的反對他的陰謀。
**殺盡了所有孩童**。很可能只殺了男孩。批評聖經記錄準確性的人注意到約瑟夫在其對希律所犯暴行的長篇記錄中，並沒有提到屠殺伯利恒嬰孩的事。據估計，在一座人口很可能不過2,000人的小鎮裏，算上其四圍的區域，也只不過會有50到60個那個年齡的孩童，並且男孩只有一半。有些人估計這人數略微高點兒。約瑟夫可能認爲，希律所犯的滔天大罪與自己相比，這事就相當小了。這種行爲確實與希律無情的性格很相符。這是希律王朝暗無天日的最後暴行之一（《歷》第六章）。而且，要是約瑟夫提到這一惡行的話，想必會對它作出說明，就像他詳細說明了所記錄的類似事件一樣。這可能就會涉及要求承認拿撒勒的耶穌是彌賽亞的論述，作爲一個猶太人，他可能决定避開這個題目。而且，由於他正在著述的是一部向羅馬人爲猶太教辯解的書，特別是向維斯帕先皇帝辯解，所以他會避免提到任何敵對羅馬的事。見本册註釋原文第75,76,94頁。
**四境**。直譯是「邊界」，因此是「區域」。在一些英文版本裏，將「四境」譯作「海岸」，而在古英語裏，「海岸」的意思就是「邊境」或「邊界」。
**兩歲**。依照在某些地區仍舊使用的東方計算方法，孩子在過了第一個歷年之後就被稱作「一歲」了，即，從其生日到下一個新年那天；在第二個歷年就「兩歲」了—即使只過了幾天或幾周。如果基督時代的猶太人這樣按照歷年計算年齡的話，就不一定可以推想他是在希律死前兩年降生的，以至爲了確保達到目標，希律就設定了「兩歲」的界限，超過了博士們所說明的時間（太2:7）。在公元前4年或者5年出生的任何一個孩子在公元前3年或者4年，即希律死的那一年，都會被稱爲「兩歲」。至於耶穌降生的大概時間，見本册註釋原文第240-242頁。

18.en: Rama. Considerable difference of opinion exists as to the identity of Rama. Several towns by this name are mentioned in the OT. It is probably to be identified with Ramallah in Ephraim, about 9 mi. (14.5 km.) northwest of Jerusalem (see Additional Note on 1 Sam. 1). This town was near the border between the tribes of Ephraim and Benjamin, the grandson and son, respectively, of Rachel, the wife of Jacob. Rachel weeping. The words of Jeremiah here cited originally referred to the bitter experiences of the Hebrew captives taken to Babylon in 586 B.C. (see on Jer. 31:15). Rachel’s death in the near vicinity, at the birth of Benjamin (Gen. 35:18–20), makes the figure particularly appropriate. She named her son Ben-oni, “son of my sorrow” (see Gen. 35:18). By inspiration Matthew applies the words of Jeremiah to Herod’s slaughter of the infants of Bethlehem (see on Deut. 18:15).
18.zh:
在拉瑪聽見號啕大哭的聲音，是拉結哭她兒女，不肯受安慰，因為他們都不在了。

**拉瑪**。關於是哪個拉瑪，存在著相當多的不同意見。在舊約中提到過幾個名爲拉瑪的城鎮。它很可能是在以法蓮的拉馬拉，在耶路撒冷西北約9英里（14.5千米）（見對撒上第一章的附註）。這個城鎮靠近以法蓮和便雅憫支派之間的邊界，以法蓮是拉結的孫子，便雅憫是拉結的兒子，拉結是雅各的妻子。
**拉結哭**。在這裏所引用的耶利米的話，最初是指希伯來人在公元前586年被擄到巴比倫的痛苦經歷（見對@耶31:15@的註釋）。拉結在生便雅憫時就死在這附近地區（創35:18-20），所以使得這個比喻特別適當。她給自己的兒子起名便俄尼，「我的悲痛之子」（見創35:18）。馬太因著靈感將耶利米的這些話應用到了希律屠殺伯利恒的嬰孩上（見對@申18:15@的註釋）。

22.en: Archelaus. In his will Herod divided his domain into four parts, giving two to Archelaus and one each to Antipas and Philip (see pp. 63-65). Archelaus proved to be the worst of the living sons of Herod. His tyranny and incompetence led the Jews and the Samaritans to appeal to Rome for his removal, which was granted in A.D. 6, tenth year of his reign. Augustus banished him to Gaul (now France), where he died. Notwithstanding. Gr. de, “and” or “but.” A dream. This was Joseph’s third recorded dream (see chs. 1:20; 2:13, 19). Turned aside. Perhaps Joseph and Mary, understanding the prophecies of the Messiah as the Son of David, had intended to take up residence in Bethlehem. Galilee. A transliteration of the Heb. meaning Galil, or Gelilah, meaning “circle,” and thus a “circuit,” or “district.” Its populace was a mixture of Jew and Gentile, and the religious prejudices of dominantly Jewish Judea were less evident there. It had no large cities. The people lived mostly in rural areas and villages, and engaged in the common, toilsome pursuits of life. Its inhabitants were despised by the residents of the more sophisticated province of Judea (John 7:52; cf. Matt. 26:69; John 1:46). From the account as given by Luke (ch. 2:39) it might appear that Joseph and Mary returned to Galilee immediately upon the presentation of Jesus at the Temple. However, Matthew makes it plain that the sojourn in Egypt intervened (see on Luke 2:39). There is no valid reason whatever for supposing the two accounts are in any way contradictory. See Palestine During the Ministry of Jesus.
22.zh:
只因聽見亞基老接著他父親希律作了猶太王，就怕往那裏去，又在夢中被主指示，便往加利利境內去了，

**亞基老**。希律在遺囑中將他的領土分地四部分，給了亞基老兩部分，安提帕和腓力各一部分（見本册註釋原文第63-65頁）。
亞基老證明是希律活著的兒子中最壞的一個。他的暴政和無能使得猶太人和撒瑪利亞人呼籲羅馬將他免職，這在他統治的第十年，公元6年得蒙准予。奧古斯都將他流放到了高盧（現在的法蘭西），他就死在那裏。
**又**。希臘文是de，「和」或「但是」。
**夢**。這是第三次記載約瑟的夢了（見太1:20；2:13,19）。
**便往**。可能約瑟和馬利亞既明白彌賽亞是大衛子孫的預言，就曾有意住在伯利恒。
**加利利**。希伯來詞Galil或Gelilah的音譯，意思是「圓周」，所以是一個「巡迴區」或「區域」。加利利的平民是猶太人和外邦人的混合，主導猶大地的猶太人的宗教偏見在這裏比較不明顯。加利利沒有大城市。百姓大多居住在鄉間和村莊裏，從事著一般的、辛苦的生活職業。加利利的居民被遠爲世故的猶大省的居民所輕視（約7:52；參太26:69；約1:46）。
根據路加福音（路2:39）的記載，似乎可能約瑟和馬利亞在聖殿爲耶穌行了奉獻禮後即刻返回了加利利。然而，馬太說明了其間還去了埃及（見對@路2:39@的註釋）。沒有任何有效的理由懷疑這兩個記錄在任何方面有矛盾。見「耶穌傳道時期的巴勒斯坦」。

1.en: When Jesus was born. [Visit of the Magi, Matt. 2:1–12. See Childhood and Youth of Jesus; the Synopsis of the Life of Christ and the Suggestive Chronology of Christ’s Birth.] Matthew mentions but briefly the fact of Jesus’ birth (ch. 1:25), and omits the various incidents connected with that event that are recorded in Luke 1:26 to Luke 2:40. Inasmuch as Matthew places emphasis on Jesus as the Messiah of OT prophecy, he proceeds to demonstrate the fact that Jesus did, in fact, fulfill all of those prophecies (see on ch. 1:22). He appears to mention, by way of introduction, chiefly such incidents connected with the infancy of Jesus as were matters of prophecy and such as pointed to the kingship of the Messiah (see chs. 1:1, 6, 17, 23; 2:2, 6, 15, 17, 18, 23). On the other hand, Luke, writing more for the Gentiles (see on ch. 1:3), emphasizes that Jesus, the Son of God (vs. 32, 35, 76), grew up and lived as a man among men in order that He might be the Saviour of all men (ch. 2:10, 14, 31, 32). For the purposes of this commentary the birth of Jesus is tentatively assigned to the autumn of 5 B.C. (see p. 240; a Synopsis of the Life of Christ and a Suggestive Chronology of Christ’s Birth). Bethlehem. Literally, “house of bread.” Its earlier name, Ephrath (Gen. 48:7), or Ephratah (Micah 5:2), means “fertility” (see on Gen. 35:19). The region of Bethlehem, its hills and valleys covered with vines, fig trees, olive groves, and grain, was probably, in part, the breadbasket of Judea. This vicinity was filled with memories for the Jewish people of Christ’s day, as it is for Christians today. It was in this area that Ruth had gleaned in the fields of Boaz (Ruth 2–4, and that David had watched his father’s flocks (1 Sam. 16:1, 11, 17:15). Here also Samuel anointed David king (1 Sam. 16:13). For further information concerning Bethlehem see on Gen. 35:19; Ruth 3:3; 4:1. See Palestine During the Ministry of Jesus. Of Judaea. To distinguish Bethlehem “of Judaea” from Bethlehem of Galilee, a town about 7 mi. (11.26 km.) northwest of Nazareth (Joshua 19:15). Herod. That is, Herod the Great (see pp. 39-42). Wise men. Gr. magoi, which designated men of the various educated classes. Our word “magicians” comes from this root. But these “wise men” were not magicians in the modern sense of sleight-of-hand performers. They were of noble birth, educated, wealthy, and influential. They were the philosophers, the counselors of the realm, learned in all the wisdom of the ancient East. The “wise men” who came seeking the Christ-child were not idolaters; they were upright, men of integrity (DA 59, 61). They studied the Hebrew Scriptures, and there found a clearer transcript of truth. In particular, the Messianic prophecies of the OT claimed their attention, and among these they found the words of Balaam: “There shall come a Star out of Jacob” (Num. 24:17). They probably also knew and understood the time prophecy of Daniel (Dan. 9:25, 26), and came to the conclusion that the Messiah’s coming was near. See pp. 61, 62. On the night of Christ’s birth a mysterious light appeared in the sky, which became a luminous star that persisted in the western heavens (see DA 60). Impressed with its import, the wise men turned once more to the sacred scrolls. As they sought to understand the meaning of the sacred writings, they were instructed in dreams to go in search of the Messiah. Like Abraham, they knew not at first where they were to go, but followed as the guiding star led them on their way. The tradition that there were but three wise men arose from the fact that there were three gifts (Matt. 2:11), and is without support in Scripture. An interesting but worthless legend gives their names as Gaspar, Balthasar, and Melchior. The unfounded idea that they were kings was deduced from Isa. 60:3 (cf. Rev. 21:24). For comment on the extent of Jewish influence throughout the Roman world of Christ’s time see pp. 59-62. From the east. The Jews regarded the regions of northern Arabia, Syria, and Mesopotamia as “east.” Thus Haran was in “the land of the people of the east” (Gen. 29:1, 4). The king of Moab later brought Balaam “from Aram [that is, Syria], out of the mountains of the east” (Num. 23:7; see on ch. 22:5). Isaiah spoke of Cyrus, the Persian, as “the righteous man from the east” (Isa. 41:2) and “a ravenous bird from the east” (ch. 46:11). Some have thought that the wise men were from the same section of the “east country” as was Balaam (see DA 59, 60), whose home has recently been identified with the Sajûr Valley between Aleppo and Carchemish, a short distance from the Euphrates (see on Num. 22:5; see also PP 438, 439). If such was the case, their journey to Bethlehem would be some 400 mi. in length and would require two or three weeks of steady travel if they rode, perhaps a month if they walked. In view of the fact that they journeyed by night in order to keep the star in view (DA 60), it may be that their traveling time was even longer. However, their point of origin may have been farther to the east, and thus their traveling distance even greater. To Jerusalem. Finally, their long journey brought them to the crest of the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. Just before dawn, perhaps, the star faded (DA 60), and soon the glistening marble dome and walls of the sacred Temple reflected the light of a new day. The fact that the wise men were directed to Jerusalem rather than to Bethlehem (DA 61) is an indication of the divine purpose that their visit should be the means of calling the attention of the leaders of the nation to the birth of the Messiah (see vs. 3–6). The attention and interest of the people were stirred as they learned of the mission of the wise men, and their minds were directed to the prophecies. Palestine Under Herod the Great 2 The leaders of the Jews were offended at the thought that the wise men were Gentiles, and refused to believe that God would pass them by in favor of men who were heathen (see DA 62, 63). For his part, Herod was enraged by the seeming indifference of the priests and scribes (vs. 3, 4), and construed the visit of the wise men to be related in some way to a plot on his own life (DA 61, 62).
1.zh:
當希律王的時候，耶穌生在猶太的伯利恒。有幾個博士從東方來到耶路撒冷，說：

**當耶穌生在**。[博士的來訪，馬太福音2:1-12。見「耶穌的童年與青年時代」；「基督生平梗概」和「基督誕生的提示性年代表」。] 馬太只是簡要地提到了耶穌降生的事（太1:25），並且省略了記載在路1:26至2:40中的與耶穌降生有關的各種事件。因爲馬太側重於說明耶穌就是舊約所預言的彌賽亞，所以他進而證明的事實就是：耶穌事實上應驗了所有那些預言（見對@太1:22@的註釋）。通過介紹，他似乎主要提到的是這種屬乎預言問題的與耶穌幼年有關的事件和這種關乎彌賽亞王權的事件（見太1:1,6,17,23；2:2,6,15,17,18,23）。另一方面，路加福音更多是寫給外邦人的（見對@路1:3@的註釋），側重於說明上帝的兒子耶穌（32,35,76節）作爲一個普通人在人們中成長與生活，以便他可以成爲所有人的救主（路2:10,14,31,32）。
本註釋將耶穌的降生暫定爲公元前5年秋（見本册註釋原文第240頁；「基督生平梗概」和「基督誕生的提示性年代表」）。
**伯利恒**。直譯是「麵包房」。它最初叫以法他（創48:7；彌5:2），意思是「肥沃」（見對@創35:19@的註釋）。伯利恒地區的丘陵和山谷遍布著葡萄樹、無花果樹、橄欖樹林和穀類，可能部分地屬於猶大主要的穀物産地。對基督時代的猶太百姓來說，這片地區充滿了回憶，它現在對基督徒也是如此。就在這片地區，路得曾在波阿斯的田裏拾麥穗（得第2-4章），大衛曾看守他父親的羊群（撒上16:1,11,17:15）。這裏還是撒母耳膏大衛爲王的地方（撒上16:13）。關於伯利恒，更多的信息見對@創35:19@；@得3:3；4:1@的註釋。見「耶穌傳道時期的巴勒斯坦」。
**猶太的**。說「猶太的」伯利恒，爲的是與加利利的伯利恒相區別，後者是拿撒勒西北（書19:15）7英里（11.26千米）左右的一個城鎮。
**希律**。即，大希律（見本册註釋原文第39-42頁）。
**博士**。希臘文是magoi，指各種受過教育的階層。這些「博士」是哲學家、王國顧問，飽學了古代東方所有的智慧。來尋求聖嬰基督的「博士們」不是拜偶像的人，而是誠實正直的人（《歷》第六章）。
他們研究了希伯來文聖經，在那裏發現了一個更加清楚的真理抄本。舊約關於彌賽亞的預言特別奪得了他們的注意，在這些預言中，他們發現了巴蘭的話：「有星要出於雅各」（民24:17）。他們很可能還知道並明白但以理的時間預言（但9:25,26），並且得出了彌賽亞即將來臨的結論。見本册註釋原文第61,62頁。
在基督降生的那晚，一道神秘的光出現在空中，它變成了一顆明亮的星停留在西部天空（見《歷》第六章）。博士們對它的重要性留有深刻的印像，就又回去查考神聖的經卷。當他們尋求明白這神聖著作的意義時，就在夢中蒙指示要去尋找彌賽亞。像亞伯拉罕一樣，他們起先並不知道往哪里去，但他們在途中却隨從了一顆路星的帶領。
因獻上三件禮物的記載（太2:11）而認爲只有三個博士的傳統說法沒有聖經依據。一個有趣但沒有價值的傳說給出了他們的名字：加斯帕、伯沙撒、和梅爾基奧（Gaspar，Balthasar，and Melchior）。認爲他們是國王的沒理由的想法是從賽60:3推斷出來的（參啟21:24）。
關於基督時代猶太人遍及羅馬勢力範圍的評論，見本册註釋原文第59-62頁。
**從東方**。猶太人把阿拉伯半島北部、叙利亞、和美索不達米亞地區都看作「東方」。所以哈蘭是在「東方人之地」（創29:1,4）。摩押王后來是「從亞蘭[即，叙利亞]」引巴蘭「出東山」的（民23:7；見對@民22:5@的註釋）。以賽亞論到波斯人古列爲「從東方來的正直人」（賽41:2）和「從東方來的鷙鳥」（賽46:11）。
有些人認爲博士們來自與巴蘭一樣的「東方國家」的同一地區（見《歷》第六章），巴蘭的家最近被鑒定在撒於爾穀（Sajûr Valley），在阿勒頗和迦基米施，距幼發拉底河很近（見對@民22:5@的註釋；另見《祖知》第四十章）。假如是這種情形的話，他們到伯利恒的行程大約就有400英里長了，如果騎馬的話需要兩到三周平穩的旅行，如果徒步旅行，可能就需要一個月的時間才能到達了。考慮到他們要不斷看到那星，就必須在夜裏旅行的事實（《歷》第六章），可能他們旅行的時間還要再長一些。然而，他們行程的起點可能在東方更遠的地區，所以他們的旅程就更長了。
**到耶路撒冷**。最後，長途旅行終於把他們帶到了耶路撒冷東部的橄欖山頂。可能就在破曉前，那星消失了（《歷》第六章），不久聖殿閃閃發光的大理石圓屋頂和墻壁就反射出了新的一天的亮光。博士們被引導到耶路撒冷而不是伯利恒的事實（《歷》第六章），表明上帝的目的是要使他們的來訪成爲一個手段，喚起國家領袖們對彌賽亞降生的注意（見第3-6節）。當百姓得知博士們的使命時，他們的注意力和興趣都被激起來了，他們的心思也被引導到了預言上。
大希律統治下的巴勒斯坦

想到這些博士是外邦人，猶太領袖們就被觸怒了，他們不相信上帝會越過他們而贊同異教徒（見《歷》第六章）。在希律這方面，他被祭司和文士們表面上漠不關心的態度激怒了（第3,4節），並且分析博士們的來訪與以某種方式謀害他的性命有關（《歷》第六章）。

5.en: Thus it is written. The quotation (v. 6) given by the chief priests and scribes does not agree entirely with either the Hebrew text of Micah 5:2 or with the LXX. It seems, rather, to be a paraphrase, or possibly from a Targum, or their own free rendering at the moment. That the import of Micah 5:2 was commonly known, even among the people, is clear from John 7:42.
5.zh:
他們回答說：「在猶太的伯利恒。因為有先知記著，說：

**因爲有先知記著說**。祭司長和文士們所引用的經文（第6節）與彌5:2的希伯來原文或七十士譯本完全一致。它似乎更是一種釋義，或者可能來自《他爾根》，要不就是他們當時作的即時翻譯。從約7:42可以清楚地看出，即使是百姓，都知識彌5:2的意思。

7.zh:
當下，希律暗暗的召了博士來，細問那星是什麼時候出現的，

**細**。更可說是：「精確地」。希律要得到詳細的信息。指的是這信息的精確性而不是指希律殷勤地尋求這信息。
**什麽時候**。希律已經從祭司長和文士們那裏得知了基督的降生地（第4-6節），現在他轉向博士們要得知基督什麽時候降生。

23.en: Nazareth. A small country town about 64 mi. (102 km.) north of Jerusalem, and between the lower end of the Sea of Galilee and the Mediterranean, on approximately the same site as the modern en–Nâṣirah. The ancient village was probably situated on the western slope rising from the floor of a depression surrounded by hilltops. The depression is pear-shaped, about a mile across, with the neck of the pear pointing southward and opening by a narrow, winding ravine into the broad plain of Esdraelon. The village was situated 1,144 ft. (c. 348 m.) above sea level, and about 920 ft. (c. 280 m.) above the plain. It lay in the territory anciently assigned to the tribe of Zebulun. See illustration facing p. 512. Some have traced the name Nazareth, or Nazareth, to a root meaning “to protect,” or “to guard,” and assign it the meaning “watchtower,” an apt description of its location high in the Galilean hills. Others derive it from a root meaning “branch” or “sprout,” which would make it a descriptive name suggestive of the dense brushwood in the hills round about. The exact form of the original name, and thus its meaning, are both uncertain. This is the first Biblical mention of Nazareth, which may imply that it was either insignificant or nonexistent in earlier times. Josephus does not include it in a list of some 200 towns and villages of Galilee. It was proverbial for its wickedness even among the people of Galilee (see on Luke 1:26). From the top of the hill above the town a magnificent view may be had in every direction. About 20 mi. (32 km.) to the west lie the blue waters of the Mediterranean. To the south is the broad, fertile plain of Esdraelon, with the mountains of Samaria beyond. About 5 mi. (8 km.) to the east rises Mt. Tabor, and in the distance, beyond the depression of the Jordan, the plateau of Gilead. To the north are the Lebanon and Anti- Lebanon mountains. The prophets. The fact that no specific prophecy resembling the one here referred to appears in the OT has led critical students of the Bible to point to this statement as an error, and therefore evidence that Matthew was not inspired. However, it is worthy of note that in previous instances where Matthew quotes a specific prophecy he speaks of “the prophet” (chs. 1:22; 2:5, 15, 17). His use of the plural form of the word “prophets” in this instance clearly implies reference, not to a particular prophetic statement, but to several, which, taken together, led to the conclusion here stated (see on Ezra 9:11; Neh. 1:8). It is possible, also, that Matthew quotes inspired writings that did not become a part of the canon of Scripture. Nazarene. Some have suggested that this name was derived from the Heb. nazir, “nazirite,” meaning “separated one,” and that Matthew’s statement originally read, “He shall be called a Nazirite” (see on Num. 6:2). But the derivation is extremely unlikely. Furthermore, Jesus was obviously not a Nazirite (Matt. 11:19; Luke 7:33, 34; cf. Num. 6:2–4). The more likely root is nasar, from which is derived neṣer, a “sprout,” “sprig,” or “shoot.” Neṣer is translated “Branch” in Isa. 11:1, a clear Messianic prophecy. The more common word for “Branch” in Messianic prophecy is ṣemach (Jer. 23:5; 33:15; Zech. 3:8; 6:12). It is possible therefore that the derivation of Nazareth from neṣer may be correct, and that the prophecies of Jesus as the “Branch” could appropriately be applied to the fact that He grew up in the city of Nazareth (see on Deut. 18:15). Others have seen in Matthew’s statement concerning Christ as a Nazarene a reference to the reproach that came, first upon the town of Nazareth, and later upon Jesus and His followers. The popular attitude toward Nazareth is evident from John 1:46; cf. ch. 7:52. The Messiah would be “despised and rejected of men” (Isa. 53:3; see also Ps. 22:6–8). Jesus was to appear, not as a celebrated ruler, but as a humble man among men. He was not even to be known as a Bethlehemite, and to have what honor might attach to Him as a citizen of the city of David. Either this or the preceding solution to the problem would seem to be in accord with Scripture.
23.zh:
到了一座城，名叫拿撒勒，就住在那裏。這是要應驗先知所說，他將稱為拿撒勒人的話了。

**拿撒勒**。耶路撒冷以北約64英里（102千米）的一個鄉鎮，在加利利海的較低端和地中海之間，與現代的en-Nâsirah約在同一位置。這個古老的村莊很可能位於從被小山頂四面環繞的窪地底部上升的西面斜坡上。這片窪地是梨形的，跨度約有一英里，梨子的頸部向南，開口處經過一個狹窄蜿蜒的溪穀進入了廣闊的耶斯列平原。這個村莊位於海平面1,144英尺（約348米）以上，比平原高出約920英尺（約280米）。它位於古時劃歸西布倫支派的領土。見本册註釋原文第512頁的圖例，。
有些人曾追溯拿撒勒這個名稱到一個意思是「保護」或「保衛」的詞根，並賦予其「守望樓」的意思，適合形容其在加利利小山高處的位置。有些人認爲它來自一個意思是「分枝」或「萌芽」的詞根，這就使它成了一個描述性名稱，使人想起周圍山間茂密的叢林。原名的確切形式及其意義都是不確定的。
這是聖經第一次提到拿撒勒，可能暗示它要麽不重要，要麽在早先的時期不存在。約瑟夫並沒有將它包括在一個加利利約200個城鎮和村莊的名單裏。即使在加利利人中，拿撒勒的邪惡也是衆所周知的（見對@路1:26@的註釋）。
從這個小鎮上面的山頂可以看到四面八方宏偉的景色。西邊約20英里（32千米）就是地中海的深海。南邊是廣闊、肥沃的耶斯列平原，遠處是撒瑪利亞群山。東邊約5英里（8千米）就是他泊山，在遠處，越過約旦盆地，就是基列高原。北邊是黎巴嫩和黎巴嫩對面的群山。
**先知**。舊約聖經中沒有出現明確的預言與這裏所提到的類似，這一事實已經使得好批評的聖經研究者們指出這句話乃是一個錯誤，還因此證明馬太福音不是上帝默示的。然而，值得注意的是，在早先的場合，馬太曾引用了說到「先知們」的一個明確的預言（太1:22；2:5,15,17）。他在本節經文使用了「先知」這個詞的複數形式，清楚地暗示了並不是指一個特別的預言陳述，而是幾個預言合到一起得到的這裏所講的結論（見對@拉9:11@；@尼1:8@的註釋）。還有可能的是，馬太引用的雖是靈感默示的著作，但並沒有成爲聖經正典的一部分。
**拿撒勒人**。有些人曾提出這個名稱來自希伯來文nazir，「拿細耳人」，意思是「分別出來的一位」，還說馬太的話最初讀作：「他將被稱爲拿細耳人」（見對@民6:2@的註釋）。但是這一詞源極爲不可能。而且，耶穌顯然不是一個拿細耳人（太11:19；路7:33,34；參民6:2-4）。更爲可能的詞根是nasar，從這個詞根洐生出了neser，一個「嫩芽」，「小枝」，或「發芽」。
Neser在賽11:1中被譯爲「枝子」，那顯然是一個關於彌賽亞的預言。在彌賽亞的預言中，更爲常見的表示「枝子」的詞是semach（耶23:5；33:15；亞3:8；6:12）。所以有可能拿撒勒來自neser是正確的，而且說耶穌好像「枝子[和合本譯爲「苗裔」]」的預言可以很適當地應用於他在拿撒勒長大的事實（見對@申18:15@的註釋）。
有些人認爲馬太關於基督是拿撒勒人的話指的是所臨到的指責，先是臨到拿撒勒鎮，後是臨到耶穌和他的跟從者身上。根據約1:46，大衆對拿撒勒的態度是顯而易見的；見約7:52。彌賽亞要「被藐視、被人厭棄」（賽53:3；另見詩22:6-8）。耶穌要顯現，不是作爲一個著名的統治者，而是作爲人群中的一個謙卑人。他甚至都不以一個伯利恒人聞名，也沒有使自己可以沾光成爲大衛之城的公民。對於這個問題，這個或前面那個解答似乎都符合聖經。

8.en: He sent them. Herod carefully concealed his own thoughts behind an exterior of professed sympathetic interest. He hoped that the wise men would return his seeming kindness. Their visit to Bethlehem would arouse no suspicion and would permit him to carry out his evil design without unnecessarily arousing the populace. The chief priests and scribes may have surmised Herod’s intent, for they knew his attitude toward pretenders to the throne. Diligently. Or, “accurately” (see on v. 7). The wise men were to press their search until they found the Messiah and verified their discovery.
8.zh:
就差他們往伯利恒去，說：「你們去仔細尋訪那小孩子，尋到了，就來報信，我也好去拜他。」

**就差他們**。希律小心地隱藏了他自己在自表同情關心的外表背後的想法。他希望博士們會回報他表面上的善意。博士們到伯利恒的訪問不會引起任何懷疑，而會使他在不激起民衆警覺的情况下執行其邪惡的計劃。祭司長和文士們可能已經猜出了希律的意圖，因爲他們很清楚他對覬覦王位者的態度。
**仔細**。或「精確地」（見對第7節的註釋）。博士們要努力尋找直到找到彌賽亞，並證實他們的發現。

6.en: Princes. The Hebrew of Micah 5:2 reads “thousands,” which may also be rendered “families,” that is, the major family subdivisions of a tribe (see on Ex. 12:37; Micah 5:2). Rule. Gr. poimainō, “to shepherd.” Isaiah had foretold that the Messiah would “feed his flock like a shepherd” (Isa. 40:11). Jesus spoke of Himself as the “good shepherd” (John 10:11, 14), Paul called Him “that great shepherd of the sheep” (Heb. 13:20), Peter, “the chief Shepherd” (1 Peter 5:4), and John, “the Lamb” that “will be their shepherd” (Rev. 7:17, RSV). Diligently. Rather, “accurately.” Herod demanded specific information. The reference is to the exactness of the information rather than to Herod’s diligence in seeking it. What time. Herod had already learned from the chief priests and the scribes where the Christ was to be born (vs. 4–6), now he turns to the wise men to learn when.
6.zh:
猶大地的伯利恒啊，你在猶大諸城中並不是最小的；因為將來有一位君王要從你那裏出來，牧養我以色列民。」

**諸城**。彌5:2的希伯來原文讀作「數千」，也可以譯爲「家族」，即，一個支派細分的主要家族（見對@出12:37@；@彌5:2@的註釋）。
**牧養**。希臘文是poimainō，「牧羊」。以賽亞曾預言過彌賽亞必「像牧人牧養自己的羊群」（賽40:11）。耶穌說到自己是「好牧人」（約10:11,14），保羅稱他是「群羊的大牧人」（來13:20），彼得稱他是「牧長」（彼前5:4），約翰稱他是「羔羊」，「必牧養他們」（啟7:17，修正標準譯本）。

15.zh:
「你們看見先知但以理所說的‘那行毀壞可憎的’站在聖地（讀這經的人須要會意）。

**那行毀壞可憎的**。見對@但9:27；11:31；12:11@的註釋。在七十士譯本中，但以理書中的這些經文含有相似的或相同的希臘詞（參馬加比一書1:54）。在猶太人中，偶像或別的異教符號經常被稱爲「可憎之物」（王上11:5,7；王下23:13等）或者某種從宗教的觀點來看是冒犯性的東西（出8:26；參創43:32；46:34等）。在路加福音中的類似段落是：「你們看見耶路撒冷被兵圍困，就可知道它成荒場的日子近了」（路21:20）。所預言的事件顯然是公元70年耶路撒冷被羅馬人毀滅的事，那時異教羅馬的像徵曾被竪立在聖殿的區域內。當公元年135猶太人在Bar Cocheba領導下的叛亂被鎮壓時，羅馬人在猶太聖殿的原址上建立了一座朱庇特神殿，並且猶太人被驅逐出耶路撒冷，違者就受死的痛苦。
**先知但以理**。這樣提到但以理證明耶穌相信但以理是一個歷史人物，是一個先知，而且寫了但以理書。因爲但以理的預言非常清楚地指出了彌賽亞出現的時間，所以在後來的數世紀中，拉比們咒詛了那些企圖計算這個時間的人（《善》第二十一章；《他勒目》Sanhedrin97b，宋西諾版，第659頁）。
**聖地**。即，聖殿的神聖區域，包括內院，是外邦人不許進入的，違者以死論處（見徒6:13；21:28）。
**讀這經的人須要會意**。那些聲稱但以理書是一本「封閉的書」，不能被人明白的人，最好思量思量基督明明說出的相反的話。當所預言的事件臨近時，上帝的子民必需知道關於那些事的預言。這些事件不到40年就會發生，是在許多當時在世之人的壽數之內的。同樣地，當與世界的末了有關的事件臨近時（見對第3節的註釋），基督徒也應該殷勤，努力明白那已爲他們寫下的警告（見摩3:7；羅15:4；林前10:11）。

19.zh:
當那些日子，懷孕的和奶孩子的有禍了。

**有禍了**。帶有小孩子的婦人會承受不住逃跑的艱苦和貧困。

2.zh:
耶穌對他們說：「你們不是看見這殿宇嗎？我實在告訴你們，將來在這裏沒有一塊石頭留在石頭上，不被拆毀了。」

**實在**。見對@太5:18@的註釋。
**一塊石頭留在石頭上**。關於聖殿所使用的一些石頭的驚人的尺寸，見對第1節的註釋。這個預言實際應驗在公元70年耶路撒冷陷落的時候（見對第1節的註釋）。
**拆毀**。約瑟夫（《猶太戰記》vi.4.5-8[249-270]）生動地描繪了聖殿的毀滅以及提多爲拯救它所做的努力。聖殿本身卓越的構造足以保證無限期地經受大自然的力量。耶路撒冷城本身實際上也是堅不可摧的，但耶穌却預言了它會被用暴力毀滅。

24.en: False Christs. See on v. 5. False prophets. See on v. 11, where false prophets prior to the fall of Jerusalem are mentioned. In this context a false prophet is a representative of a false messiah. For more detailed counsel with respect to such prophets see on ch. 7:15–23. Great signs. See p. 208; see on Luke 2:12. False prophets perform “signs” as proof of their authority, and these are seen by the people as “wonders” (see p. 208; see on Matt. 12:38, 39). For a more specific reference to some of the important “signs” performed by these latter-day prophets, see Rev. 13:13, 14; 16:13, 14; 19:20. However, these false miracles lack the power of God.
